title: AI Generated Synthetic Electrocardiograms Demonstrate Morphological Preservation
authors: Simon Eggleton; B. Gallego; J. Ryan
model_family: GAN (WGAN-GP, EMA-averaged generator weights)
task: class-specific synthesis (acute aortic dissection ECGs for augmentation)
datasets: MIMIC-IV-ECG (197 acute aortic dissection ECGs, simple-augmented to 4,956 training ECGs; 60 held-out AAD ECGs for comparison)
loss_functions: WGAN-GP (Wasserstein adversarial loss + gradient penalty)
loss_families: Adversarial (GAN); WGAN / gradient penalty
eval_metrics: amplitude statistics (signal SD, peak-to-peak amplitude, global signal energy) with significance tests; power spectral density comparison by frequency band; DTW
metric_families: DTW; Spectral / PSD similarity; Statistical tests
notes: Conference abstract only (HLC 2026 supplement, abstract 0586). 60 synthetic vs 60 held-out real AAD ECGs: synthetic SD 17.1% lower (p<0.001), peak-to-peak +0.7%, signal energy 17.8% lower; PSD similar in 5-150 Hz with deviations at extremes; DTW 1.30. No downstream utility, no baseline, no reference real-real DTW, and alignment/pairing of synthetic to real ECGs is unspecified.
takeaway: Simple amplitude-distribution statistics (per-record SD, peak-to-peak, energy with effect sizes) detected variance shrinkage that DTW did not, so ECGEN-Eval should report such amplitude-spread summaries next to dtw/psd.

title: AI modeling photoplethysmography to electrocardiography useful for predicting cardiovascular disease
authors: Zhengyao Ding; Yujian Hu; Ziyu Li; Yiheng Mao; Haitao Li; Dongchen Zhou; Xuesen Chu; Yu Long; Ziyi Liu; Fei Wu; Hongkun Zhang; Qingbo Xu
model_family: AR-Transformer (TimeVQVAE-style: STFT dual-band LF/HF VQ-VAE + bidirectional masked-token Transformers, PPG-conditioned via CLIP-style contrastive PPG encoder); Hybrid
task: PPG2ECG
data_type: Single-lead ECG; Wearable / ambulatory ECG; Multimodal (ECG + other signals)
data_format: Raw waveform segment; Time-frequency (spectrogram / wavelet); Latent / tokenised
datasets: PulseDB-MIMIC; PulseDB-VitalDB; MESA (pretraining); MIMIC-AF subset; private BBX smart-ring PPG-AF set; PPG-DaLiA; WESAD
loss_functions: Stage 0: symmetric InfoNCE/CLIP contrastive loss (PPG-ECG, τ=0.05) + MAE reconstruction pretraining; Stage 1: VQ codebook + β-commitment loss + L2 reconstruction (ISTFT) for LF and HF; Stage 2: masked-token negative log-likelihood (cross-entropy) for LF/HF priors
loss_families: L2 / MSE reconstruction; Classification CE; Spectral / frequency; Contrastive / CLIP; VQ / codebook; Token cross-entropy
eval_metrics: FID (on ROCKET features); Fréchet Distance on raw signals (FD); Marginal Distribution Difference (MDD); Autocorrelation Difference (ACD); Skewness Difference (SD); Kurtosis Difference (KD); MAE; MSE; PSNR; SSIM; downstream CVD screening AUC, sensitivity, specificity, accuracy, PPV, NPV, F1, kappa (DeLong, McNemar, bootstrap)
metric_families: Cross-dataset / external validation; Downstream classification; FID / embedding Fréchet; MAE; Other: TSGBench statistical differences; PSNR / SNR; SSIM
robustness: External validation on independent PPG-AF dataset recorded by consumer smart ring (two channels separately) and out-of-domain generalization; label-efficiency analysis. Limitations note geographically homogeneous training populations.
embedding_extractor: ROCKET random-convolution features for FID
notes: Uses TSGBench-style stats (MDD, ACD, SD, KD) alongside FID/FD/PSNR/SSIM; baselines RDDM, WGAN, RecQRS. ACD 0.367 vs 31.0 second-best; FID 0.001 vs 0.008. Primary aim is CVD prediction from PPG; generation is for interpretability.
takeaway: Add cheap time-series distribution stats (marginal-distribution, autocorrelation, skewness, kurtosis differences) and a ROCKET-feature FID variant.

title: AI-based 3-Lead to 12-Lead ECG Reconstruction: Towards Smartphone-based Public Healthcare
authors: Aditya Mallick; Rahul L R; Albert Shaiju; Satya Deepika Neelapala; Lopamudra Giri; Rahuldeb Sarkar; Soumya Jana
model_family: GAN (1D Pix2Pix conditional GAN, UNet generator, PatchGAN-style 1D interval discriminator); baselines LSTM, LSTM-UNet
task: lead-reconstruction (3-lead I, II, V2 -> 12-lead)
datasets: Train: SPH (Shaoxing), CPSC2018, Georgia, INCART; Test: PTB, PTB-XL
loss_functions: not explicitly reported (1D Pix2Pix conditional adversarial objective implied)
loss_families: Adversarial (GAN)
eval_metrics: coefficient of determination R2; Pearson correlation coefficient rx; per-lead and per-diagnostic-subgroup (HC, BB, HY, MI, VA, ND) analysis
metric_families: Cross-dataset / external validation; Other: per-diagnosis performance breakdown; Pearson / correlation; R² (coefficient of determination)
robustness: Cross-patient/cross-database evaluation: trained on SPH, CPSC, Georgia, INCART and tested on held-out PTB and PTB-XL databases; compared with personalized models.
notes: Public (cross-patient) vs personalized setting comparison. R2 84.8%/rx 93.2% on PTB-XL vs LSTM-UNet 74.6%/86.0%. Leads V4-V6 hardest. Pitfall: early stopping on highest R2 on the test dataset. R2 formula as printed is non-standard.
takeaway: Report reconstruction metrics per lead and per diagnostic subgroup; R2 + Pearson are standard paired metrics for lead reconstruction.

title: An Innovative Approach for Long ECG Synthesis with Wasserstein GAN Model
authors: Thi Diem Tran; Thi Thu Khiet Dang; Ngoc Quoc Tran
venue: Lecture Notes in Computer Science (ICCSA 2024, LNCS 14814)
model_family: GAN (DCGAN with WGAN-GP on 2D binary line-plot images of ECG; image-to-signal column-search extraction)
task: class-wise synthesis (beat classes N/S/V/F and 10 s rhythms NSR/VT/SVT) via signal-to-image; augmentation
data_format: ECG image; Single heartbeats; Raw waveform segment
datasets: MIT-BIH Arrhythmia (lead II, DS1/DS2 split); European ST-T; Chapman (Zheng et al. 12-lead, 10646 patients)
loss_functions: WGAN-GP (lambda = 10)
loss_families: WGAN / gradient penalty
eval_metrics: MSE; RMSE/NRMSE; SSIM; cross-correlation coefficient (beats vs DS2 / MIT test beats); CNN beat classifier ACC/SEN/SPEC trained on real, synthetic, and real+synthetic (TSTR-like and augmentation); visual comparison with LSTM-GAN, WGAN-GP 1D, TTS-GAN, S12-ECG-GAN, DDPM; Pan-Tompkins R-peak overlay for 10 s signals; generation time (≈30 s vs ≈2 min DDPM per sample)
metric_families: Augmentation gain; Efficiency (NFE / runtime / params); MSE; Pearson / correlation; RMSE; SSIM; TSTR / TRTS; Visual inspection (qualitative)
notes: One-beat (MIT DS1+DS2): MSE 0.00179, RMSE 0.0237, SSIM 0.9978, CC 0.9546 (vs 0.00241/0.0292/0.9977/0.9425 for ECG-Adv-GAN). Augmentation raises beat-classifier ACC from 99.31 to 99.78 (MIT 80/20) and 97.72 to 98.32 (DS1→DS2). 10 s rhythm synthesis is assessed only visually (no quantitative metric); pairing of synthetic vs real beats for MSE/SSIM is not described, and amplitude is lost in the binary-image representation.
takeaway: Long-ECG (10 s rhythm) papers still lack quantitative evaluation, so ECGEN-Eval's heart_rate, hrv and feature-extractor RR distributions should be promoted as the standard rhythm-level metrics, with nearest-neighbour pairing made explicit for mse/ssim-style scores.

title: Applying Generative Models and Transfer Learning to Physiological Data Classification
authors: José Fernando Núñez; Jamie Arjona; Adrián Tormos; Dario García-Gasulla; Javier Béjar
venue: Frontiers in artificial intelligence and applications
model_family: GAN + Diffusion (class-conditional 1D-CNN GAN with patch discriminator; TTS-CGAN transformer GAN; DiffWave-based diffusion with cross-attention label conditioning)
task: class-cond (beat augmentation and synthetic pretraining / transfer learning)
datasets: MIT-BIH Arrhythmia (5 AAMI classes); PTB Diagnostic ECG (MI vs healthy); Kachuee et al. preprocessed beat segments
loss_functions: adversarial GAN loss + auxiliary classification output in discriminator (AC-GAN style); DiffWave denoising objective
loss_families: Adversarial (GAN); Diffusion noise prediction; Classification CE
eval_metrics: t-SNE plots; LLE plots; TSTR; TRTS; TRTR; TSTS; TRSTR (accuracy, precision, recall); synthetic pretraining + fine-tuning with 20-100% real data; cross-task transfer (MIT-BIH synthetic -> PTB MI); training time
metric_families: Augmentation gain; Downstream classification; Efficiency (NFE / runtime / params); TSTR / TRTS; t-SNE / UMAP / PCA plots
notes: TSTR accuracy only 0.551 (MIT) / 0.660 (PTB) vs TRTR 0.980 / 0.914 while TSTS ~1.0, i.e. synthetic classes are over-separated 'simplified' beats; synthetic-MIT pretraining then PTB fine-tuning raises accuracy 0.890 -> 0.964. DiffWave best covers the real distribution in t-SNE, TTS-CGAN best for pretraining; authors conclude t-SNE/LLE and classifier scores are insufficient and call for better time-series evaluation metrics.
takeaway: Report TSTS alongside TSTR as a cheap 'over-separation' diagnostic (TSTS ~1.0 with low TSTR flags simplified class-prototype samples) and complement ECGEN-Eval's pr_dist/nn_dist with an embedding plot, since this paper shows visual t-SNE and utility alone are insufficient.

title: Are AI-generated electrocardiograms clinically accurate? Benchmarking accuracy of AI-generated ECGs: a multiplatform performance study of public LLMs
authors: H. Kamalanathan; A Vuong; Stephen Bacchi; Shaun Evans; Joshua George Kovoor; A Gupta; Victor Theophilus Premkumar; Ash Wilson-Smith; David Downes; Kyrillos Kaleeny; P Sahai; J.D.S Millhouse
model_family: EvalOnly (public text-to-image/LLM platforms: Bard, Bing Image Creator, DALL-E)
task: evaluation (text-cond ECG image generation by general-purpose AI)
datasets: 113 AI-generated ECG images (10 rhythms x 3 platforms x 4, after exclusions)
loss_functions: not applicable
eval_metrics: Blinded expert rhythm diagnosis by 3 physicians incl. cardiologist with adjudication; accuracy = agreement with prompted rhythm; proportion uninterpretable
metric_families: Expert / Turing test; Label / condition adherence
eval_categories: Privacy; Clinical validity; Human / expert; Conditional consistency
privacy: Notes Bard mostly retrieved existing online ECG images rather than generating them (retrieval/copying), observed qualitatively; no formal memorisation metric.
notes: Conference abstract. Only 32.7% of 113 ECGs matched intended rhythm; 25.1% uninterpretable. Bard 84.5% correct but mostly retrieved existing online images (memorisation/retrieval pitfall). AFL 58.3%, AF 50% best.
takeaway: Label-consistency (does generated ECG match prompted class?) via expert or classifier, plus retrieval/memorisation check, is essential for conditional generators.

title: Assessing the robustness of evaluation metrics for synthetic ECG signal quality
authors: Maria Russo; Inês Sousa; Ricardo Santos; Joana Rebelo; Fabiana Martins Clemente; Gonçalo Ribeiro; André Carreiro; Marília Barandas
model_family: EvalOnly (benchmarks SSSD-ECG diffusion, conditional WaveGAN* and Pulse2Pulse GANs, cNVAE-ECG hierarchical VAE, YData proprietary TimeSeriesSynthesizer)
task: evaluation (metric robustness under controlled perturbations of class-conditional 12-lead synthetic ECGs)
datasets: PTB-XL (21,837 records, 71 SCP statements; folds 1-8 train, 9 val, 10 test)
loss_functions: not applicable (evaluation study; XResNet1d50 utility classifier trained with binary cross-entropy)
loss_families: Adversarial (GAN); Classification CE
eval_metrics: Kolmogorov-Smirnov test (per-feature); Range Coverage; Improved Precision; Density; Improved Recall; Coverage; Distance to Closest Record (DCR); Authenticity; TSTR macro-AUROC (XResNet1d50, 71 labels); class-wise AUROC; UMAP projections; robustness curves under 5 perturbations (magnitude warp, amplitude scaling, time warp, Gaussian noise mixing, frequency band attenuation) x 10 intensities x 5 seeds
metric_families: Downstream classification; Nearest-neighbour / DCR distance; Noise / perturbation robustness; Other: Range coverage; Precision / recall / density / coverage; Statistical tests; TSTR / TRTS; t-SNE / UMAP / PCA plots
robustness: Core contribution: metrics are stress-tested under five controlled perturbation types at ten intensities; density and coverage behave robustly, KS/range coverage/IR/privacy/macro-AUROC do not reflect morphological degradation, and all feature-based metrics miss time warping.
privacy: DCR and authenticity are reported; they increase with any distortion (fidelity-privacy trade-off), so the authors argue privacy metrics cannot be judged for robustness alone and must be read jointly with fidelity.
embedding_extractor: TSFEL handcrafted statistical/spectral/temporal features extracted per lead (metrics via YData evaluation framework and pyMDMA)
notes: SSSD-ECG best (KS 0.812, IP 0.968, density 0.992, IR 0.835, coverage 0.718, DCR 0.705, TSTR macro-AUROC 0.835 vs TRTR 0.919); GANs collapse (coverage 0.012 P2P, 0.022 WaveGAN*). Under perturbation, density (fidelity) and coverage (diversity) degrade progressively and interpretably (e.g. density 0.98->0.48 when 5-30 Hz QRS band removed; coverage 0.69->0.14 at 50% noise), whereas KS/range coverage are insensitive, Improved Recall rises artificially, privacy metrics trivially rise with distortion, and TSTR macro-AUROC stays flat until severe corruption. All feature-space metrics are blind to time warping because TSFEL features are amplitude-dominated.
takeaway: Report density and coverage alongside pr_dist (precision/recall), add a built-in perturbation-sanity test (magnitude/time warp, noise mixing, band-stop) to verify each metric responds monotonically, and caveat that nn_dist/privacy scores improve with any degradation and must be read jointly with fidelity.

title: Autoencoder-based Arrhythmia Detection using Synthetic ECG Generation Technique
authors: Ali Nawaz; Mubarak Albarka Umar; Khaled Shuaib; Amir Ahmad; Abdelkader Nasreddine Belkacem
venue: Annual International Conference of the IEEE Engineering in Medicine and Biology Society (EMBC)
model_family: GAN (TabGAN tabular GAN treating each beat as a feature row) + dense autoencoder anomaly detector
task: unconditional (normal-beat synthesis for augmentation of AE anomaly detector)
datasets: MIT-BIH Arrhythmia (Kaggle-style preprocessed heartbeat set, 109,446 beats, 5 AAMI classes)
loss_functions: standard TabGAN adversarial loss; AE reconstruction loss
loss_families: Adversarial (GAN)
eval_metrics: AUC-ROC and AUC-PR of AE anomaly detector trained on real normal + 5x/10x synthetic normal beats; comparison with DAGMM, GMM, iForest, LOF
metric_families: Augmentation gain; Downstream classification
notes: AUC-ROC 0.656 -> 0.677 (5x) -> 0.686 (10x), AUC-PR 0.826 -> 0.854 -> 0.867; still below DAGMM 0.762. No direct signal-fidelity, distribution or visual evaluation of the synthetic beats; despite the abstract, Algorithm 1 trains the AE on synthetic + real normal data (augmentation, not pure train-on-synthetic); a generic tabular GAN ignores temporal structure.
takeaway: An example of utility-only evaluation of a generic tabular GAN; ECGEN-Eval reports should always pair downstream gains with direct fidelity/diversity metrics (mmd, pr_dist, hrv, sqi) so beat realism is not inferred from a small anomaly-detection AUC change.

title: Bayesian ECG reconstruction using denoising diffusion generative models
authors: Gabriel V. Cardoso; Lisa Bedin; Josselin Duchateau; Rémi Dubois; Eric Moulines
model_family: Diffusion (conditional DDGM/DDPM, EDM-like U-Net; 'ECGDiff') used as Bayesian prior via MCGdiff SMC posterior sampling
task: class-cond (healthy beat conditioned on age, sex, RR); imputation (missing-lead reconstruction); denoising; anomaly detection
conditioning: Patient attributes (age, sex, ...); Other ECG leads
datasets: PhysioNet/CinC Challenge 2021 (43,101 records; 28,167 patients normal beats, 468 MI patients)
loss_functions: DDPM denoising objective (equivalent to KL between inference and backward processes); no adversarial loss
loss_families: Adversarial (GAN); Diffusion noise prediction; KL / ELBO
eval_metrics: Earth Mover's Distance (EMD, L2 transport cost on ECG concatenated with age/sex/RR) generated vs test/train; out-of-distribution uncertainty via random-network-distillation-style ResNet pairs (B=10); rescaled Mahalanobis distance of posterior; R² score for missing-lead reconstruction vs Dower matrix; R² for QT-vs-RR vs Bazett/Fridericia/Framingham; ROC for MI detection
metric_families: Clinical intervals (PR/QRS/QT/ST); Downstream classification; Metric sensitivity analysis; Noise / perturbation robustness; Other: out-of-distribution uncertainty; R² (coefficient of determination); Wasserstein / EMD
eval_categories: Fidelity; Utility; Fairness; Robustness; Clinical validity; Conditional consistency
fairness: MI detection ROC reported separately for males (AUC 0.75) and females (0.70); controls sampled to match MI age-by-sex distribution.
robustness: EMD error bars over training batches and noisy-test vs train reference; denoising under Gaussian noise of varying per-lead SD; sensitivity of EMD to SMC particle number.
embedding_extractor: randomly initialised + trained ResNet pair (RND-style uncertainty), not a pretrained classifier
notes: Proposes two 'novel' metrics: global EMD (with conditioning features in transport cost; compared gen-vs-test against test-vs-train baseline) and per-sample out-of-support uncertainty. Missing-lead R² 0.98-0.99 vs Dower 0.71-0.87. Amplitude-normalised beats, so amplitude fidelity is not evaluated.
takeaway: Adopt EMD with real-vs-real (train vs test) reference baseline, and a per-sample out-of-support/novelty score.

title: Beyond Single-Channel: Multichannel Signal Imaging for PPG-to-ECG Reconstruction with Vision Transformers
authors: Xiaoyan Li; Shixin Xu; Faisal Habib; Arvind Gupta; Huaxiong Huang
model_family: Other (ViT encoder-decoder on four-channel PPG signal images; deterministic regression)
task: PPG2ECG
datasets: BIDMC PPG and Respiration; CapnoBase
loss_functions: MSE reconstruction loss on ECG image + QRS-complex-enhanced loss (Gaussian weighting around R-peaks, params sigma, beta); total = sum
loss_families: L2 / MSE reconstruction; Physiology / physics
eval_metrics: PRD; RMSE; HRV of RR, PP, TT intervals (R-HRV, P-HRV, T-HRV, mean/STD differences); QRS area relative error; PR interval relative error; RT interval relative error; RT amplitude-difference relative error
metric_families: Clinical intervals (PR/QRS/QT/ST); Heart rate / HRV; PRD / normalised PRD; RMSE
notes: Introduces clinically-oriented paired metrics (QRS area, PR interval, RT interval, RT amplitude errors). Only 30 low-noise records chosen because peak detection is unreliable on noisy P waves (selection bias). BIDMC PRD 42.65 vs CLEP-GAN 71.43. R/P/T-HRV values identical in table (suspicious).
takeaway: Clinical interval/amplitude relative-error metrics (PR, QRS area, RT) map well onto the features module for paired evaluation.

title: Boosting EEG and ECG Classification with Synthetic Biophysical Data Generated via Generative Adversarial Networks
authors: Archana Venugopal; Diego R. Faria
model_family: GAN (WGAN-GP; also vanilla GAN baseline)
task: augmentation (EEG mental states; ECG normal/abnormal)
datasets: ECG: Kaggle ECG dataset (140-point beats, normal/abnormal labels); EEG: Bird et al. Muse dataset (TP9, AF7, AF8, TP10)
loss_functions: WGAN-GP: critic loss D(fake)-D(real)+lambda*GP (lambda=10); generator -D(fake); post-hoc smoothing (window 10) of synthetic ECG
loss_families: WGAN / gradient penalty
eval_metrics: classification accuracy (SVM, RF) trained on real tested on real/synthetic/combined, and with real+synthetic training at varying synthetic proportions; PSD plots (EEG); visual inspection
metric_families: Augmentation gain; Statistical tests; TSTR / TRTS; Visual inspection (qualitative)
notes: ECG RF accuracy 97% real -> 98.40% with synthetic. Train-on-real/test-on-synthetic (TRTS) used as quality check. Post-hoc smoothing applied to remove GAN spikes, which may mask generator artefacts. No distributional metrics.
takeaway: TRTS (classifier trained on real, tested on synthetic) is a cheap complementary utility metric; flag post-processing that hides artefacts.

title: Can Diffusion Models Understand the Long Term Dependencies in an ECG?
authors: Dominik D. Kranz; Oruç Kahriman; Niels Wessel; Jan F. Kraemer
model_family: Diffusion (latent diffusion: VQ-VAE on 2 s windows, latent 32x8 per window, concatenated over 320 s; DDIM denoiser)
task: unconditional (long 320 s single-lead ECG); inpainting showcased
datasets: Synthetic training set only: 3,456 noise-free 320 s ECGs rendered from ECGSYN beat-to-beat interval series with a library of idealised QRS complexes
loss_functions: not reported (standard VQ-VAE + DDIM denoising objectives implied)
loss_families: Diffusion noise prediction; VQ / codebook
eval_metrics: HRV parameters (time/frequency domain, incl. VLF/LF/HF spectrum) compared to training set; cumulative distribution of HRV parameters; mean heart-rate distribution (training vs generated, 3,456 each); rate of misrendered QRS complexes; visual inspection
metric_families: Heart rate / HRV; Physiological validity rate; Visual inspection (qualitative)
notes: ~30% of generated 320 s ECGs had >=1 misrendered QRS, producing ~1 s BBI gaps and spurious VLF HRV power; mean HR 70.91 (real) vs 70.67 BPM (generated) but distribution tails under-represented, visible only in cumulative distributions over 3,456 samples. Training data were themselves synthetic (ECGSYN), so no real-ECG evaluation; 2-s VQ-VAE window seams caused periodic disturbances every 2048 samples. 2-page workshop abstract, no baselines.
takeaway: Report full distribution/tail comparisons (e.g. quantile or KS on per-recording HR/HRV, not just means) and add a beat-validity check (fraction of recordings with missed/misrendered QRS or implausible RR gaps) since a single bad beat corrupts HRV metrics.

title: CardioFlow: Learning to Generate ECG from PPG with Rectified Flow
authors: Yuta Nambu; Masahiro Kohjima; Ryûji Yamamoto
venue: IEEE International Conference on Acoustics Speech and Signal Processing
model_family: FlowMatching (conditional rectified flow, RDDM-style 1D velocity network, Euler sampling 1-50 steps, probabilistic QRS/systolic-peak masks)
task: PPG→ECG translation
datasets: WESAD; PPG-DaLiA (15 subjects each; subject-independent 9/3/3 split)
loss_functions: rectified-flow velocity regression ||(x1 - x0) - v(xt, t, c)|| with masked ECG/PPG (mask prob q=0.3, window L=32)
loss_families: Flow-matching velocity
eval_metrics: RMSE; Fréchet distance (FD); heart-rate MAE (Hamilton QRS detector, 8 s windows); sampling time vs number of steps; downstream 3-class stress/emotion recognition accuracy and F1 (Transformer classifier) on WESAD; qualitative plots
metric_families: Curve Fréchet distance; Downstream classification; Efficiency (NFE / runtime / params); Heart rate / HRV; RMSE; Visual inspection (qualitative)
eval_categories: Fidelity; Utility; Robustness; Clinical validity; Conditional consistency; Efficiency
robustness: Evaluated on DaLiA (exercise, weaker PPG-ECG correlation) as a harder setting, subject-independent split.
notes: WESAD: RMSE 0.24 / FD 10.4 / HR-MAE 5.1 bpm (RDDM 0.21/7.2/6.9, DDPM 0.27/16.5/9.5); DaLiA: 0.22/8.8/7.5 (RDDM 0.19/7.8/10.4); emotion recognition Acc 0.64/F1 0.58 vs real ECG 0.66/0.61 and PPG 0.55/0.47; good HR-MAE already at ~10 steps. Authors note RMSE/FD reward low-amplitude QRS and penalise misaligned but correct beats, motivating HR-based clinical metrics alongside paired waveform errors.
takeaway: For paired translation tasks, report a paired heart-rate/R-peak agreement metric (HR MAE from detected beats) next to RMSE/FD, and caveat that point-wise errors reward flattened QRS complexes.

title: CDM-DL-PSI: A conditional diffusion model for 12-Lead ECG generation using disease labels and patient-specific information
authors: Rongjia Wang; Xunde Dong; Xiuling Liu; Fei Hu
model_family: Diffusion (latent diffusion: conv/self-attention AE + S4-based noise predictor with 36 RCGFM blocks, adaLN-Zero for timestep and MCFARN multi-condition modulation)
task: class-cond + patient attributes (multi-label disease + age + sex) 12-lead synthesis
conditioning: Class / diagnosis label; Patient attributes (age, sex, ...)
datasets: PTB-XL (21,506 records, 5 superclasses); CPSC2018 (6,868 records, 9 classes); Chapman (transfer/fine-tuning only)
loss_functions: AE: MSE reconstruction; noise predictor: epsilon-MSE + lambda=0.1 frequency (Fourier) loss between clean and predicted latent z0
loss_families: L2 / MSE reconstruction; Diffusion noise prediction; Spectral / frequency
eval_metrics: RMSE; DTW distance; spectral coherence (SC); coverage score (CS); distribution recall (DR); TRTS 'fidelity' (Acc/F1/AUC, train real test generated) and TSTR 'diversity' (Acc/F1/AUC) with 4 classifiers (XResNet1d50, InceptionTime, MVMS-Net, MRTNet); clinical Turing test (10 cardiologists); age-prediction MAE and sex-classification accuracy on generated ECG; memory footprint, training time, inference time; condition-perturbation robustness; Chapman transfer
metric_families: DTW; Demographic attribute preservation; Efficiency (NFE / runtime / params); Expert / Turing test; Noise / perturbation robustness; Precision / recall / density / coverage; RMSE; Spectral / PSD similarity; TSTR / TRTS
eval_categories: Fidelity; Diversity; Utility; Robustness; Human / expert; Conditional consistency; Efficiency
robustness: Robustness to missing or 30%-corrupted conditioning (labels, sex, age +/-10 y) assessed via signal/distribution metrics; generalisation tested by fine-tuning label embeddings to the Chapman dataset.
embedding_extractor: not specified for CS/DR (cluster-based coverage per ref [73]); ResNet age/sex predictors for attribute consistency
notes: PTB-XL: RMSE 0.2531, DTW 92.84, SC 0.1711, CS 1.00, DR 1.00; TRTS (XResNet) F1 70.20 vs real baseline 72.77, TSTR F1 66.40 / AUC 85.59 (best of SSSD-ECG, DSAT-ECG, FlowECG, WaveGAN, Pulse2Pulse); Turing test cardiologist accuracy 62.3% (WaveGAN 79.3%); age MAE 7.70 vs 7.31 real, sex Acc 82.72 vs 83.73; 12 s per ECG, 4.96 GB. DR is 1.00 for every model (saturated by matching generated counts to real per cluster) and SC between two real ECGs is only ~0.20, so these signal-level metrics barely discriminate models; RMSE/DTW pairing to the label-source record is implied, not stated.
takeaway: Add an attribute-consistency check (age-regressor MAE / sex-classifier accuracy on generated vs real ECG) for patient-conditioned generators, and flag saturated or non-discriminative metrics (e.g. recall = 1.0 for all models, coherence near the real-vs-real floor) by always reporting a real-vs-real reference value alongside each score.

title: Classification feasibility test on multi-lead electrocardiography signals generated from single-lead electrocardiography signals
authors: Gi-Won Yoon; Segyeong Joo
model_family: GAN (pix2pix conditional GAN, U-Net generator, 1-D; 11 per-lead models)
task: lead-reconstruction
datasets: Asan Medical Center MUSE database (training, ~4M records); PTB-XL (external, classification)
loss_functions: cGAN adversarial loss + L1 reconstruction loss (pix2pix objective G* = argmin max L_cGAN + L_L1)
loss_families: Adversarial (GAN); L1 reconstruction
eval_metrics: Downstream ResNet classification precision; recall; F1-score; accuracy; ROC/AUC (6 classes: normal, AF, LBBB, RBBB, LVH, RVH) comparing generated 12-lead vs real 12-lead vs real lead I; Einthoven-derived lead ablations
metric_families: Inter-lead consistency; TSTR / TRTS
robustness: Classification utility evaluated on external PTB-XL dataset not used to train the generator (trained on Asan Medical Center data).
notes: Generation fidelity (FD, MSE) evaluated in prior work; here utility only. Surprising: generated 12-lead F1 0.81 > real 12-lead 0.70 on PTB-XL; authors suggest FD/MSE plus Turing test needed. Mixed-in Einthoven-formula leads gave no significant difference.
takeaway: Utility comparison vs. the single-lead input baseline is a useful 'information gain' check for lead-reconstruction models.

title: Classification of ECG Signals Using GAN, SMOTE, and VAE Data Augmentation Methods: Synthetic vs. Real
authors: Turgut Özseven
venue: Bitlis Eren Üniversitesi Fen Bilimleri Dergisi
model_family: GAN (vanilla GAN, 2D conv) and VAE (2-layer CNN encoder/decoder) compared with SMOTE
task: augmentation (class-imbalanced heartbeat classification)
datasets: MIT-BIH Arrhythmia (MLII lead, 4 AAMI classes F/N/S/V, 42 records)
loss_functions: standard minimax GAN loss (Goodfellow); VAE (reparameterization; loss not explicitly stated)
loss_families: Adversarial (GAN)
eval_metrics: accuracy; specificity; recall; F1-score of a 2D-CNN classifier under real-only, synthetic-only, train-synthetic-test-real, and real+synthetic settings
metric_families: Augmentation gain; Downstream classification; TSTR / TRTS
notes: Heartbeats processed as 2D images. Real-only 96.5%; synthetic-only (VAE) 100% (train and test on synthetic, trivially optimistic); TSTR best 86.4% with SMOTE; real+synthetic best 98.6% (VAE). No direct fidelity metrics. Patient-dependent (beat-level) split risks leakage.
takeaway: Shows why TSTR must be separated from train/test-on-synthetic; enforce patient-level splits in utility evaluation.

title: Classification of imbalanced ECGs through segmentation models and augmented by conditional diffusion model
authors: Jinhee Kwak; Jaehee Jung
model_family: Diffusion (conditional DDPM, U-Net, classifier-free guidance; 1-D reshaped to 2-D) compared with VAE and SMOTE-Tomek
task: augmentation (class-cond beats for imbalanced arrhythmia classification)
datasets: MIT-BIH Arrhythmia (AAMI N/S/V/F, records 102/104/107/217 excluded)
loss_functions: DDPM L_simple noise-prediction MSE; VAE baseline: reconstruction + KL (ELBO)
loss_families: L2 / MSE reconstruction; Diffusion noise prediction; KL / ELBO
eval_metrics: Cosine similarity between true and predicted noise on test set (diffusion) / between reconstructed and original (VAE); visual morphology inspection; downstream CNN/transformer classifier Precision, Sensitivity, F1, Accuracy, confusion matrix
metric_families: Augmentation gain; Cosine similarity; Visual inspection (qualitative)
notes: Weak generative evaluation: cosine similarity of predicted vs true noise is a training-loss proxy, not a sample-quality metric. Augmentation gave +1.23% F1 for minority classes. Mentions prior VAE work using MMD (3.83e-3).
takeaway: Illustrates pitfall of using denoising-loss proxies as quality metrics; ECGEN-Eval should promote sample-level distribution metrics instead.

title: Classifier-Guided Diffusion Model for Generating Disease-Specific ECG Data: A Case Pilot Study on Inferior Myocardial Infarction
authors: Hongtao Chen; Shota Kato; Kana Eguchi; Tetsuma Kawaji; Manabu Kano
venue: Annual International Conference of the IEEE Engineering in Medicine and Biology Society (EMBC 2025)
model_family: Diffusion (DDPM, 1D U-Net, trained on normal ECGs only; classifier guidance with CNN normal-vs-IMI classifier, w = 30)
task: class-cond (inferior MI) via classifier guidance; augmentation / substitution
datasets: PTB-XL (lead II, 100 Hz; 9514 normal, 3271 IMI records)
loss_functions: simplified DDPM noise-prediction MSE (1000 steps, beta 1e-4..2e-3); cross-entropy for guidance classifier
loss_families: L2 / MSE reconstruction; Diffusion noise prediction; Classification CE
eval_metrics: Normal-vs-IMI classification precision and F1 when real IMI is partly/fully replaced by synthetic IMI (Merge1-3); Q-wave depth (Q/R ratio) distribution of real normal vs real IMI vs generated IMI (histogram); visual annotated PQRST of generated sample
metric_families: Clinical intervals (PR/QRS/QT/ST); Downstream classification; Expert / Turing test; Visual inspection (qualitative)
eval_categories: Fidelity; Utility; Clinical validity; Human / expert; Conditional consistency
notes: Real-only baseline precision 0.919 / F1 0.761; Merge1 (1000 synthetic IMI) 0.925 / 0.792; Merge3 (all IMI synthetic) 0.911 / 0.744. Generated IMI Q/R ratio peaks ~0.35 vs ~0.25 for real IMI (normal 0-0.1). Caveats: 1000 'high-quality' samples hand-screened from 30000 generations (no rejection rate reported as a metric), and the merged datasets were split 7:2:1 so test sets contain synthetic IMI, i.e. not a TSTR on real test data; no fidelity/distribution metric beyond one histogram.
takeaway: ECGEN-Eval's feature extractor could add pathology-targeted features (Q/R ratio, Q-wave duration) compared as real-vs-synthetic distributions per class, and reports should state any post-hoc sample filtering and its acceptance rate.

title: CLEP-GAN: An Innovative Approach to Subject-Independent ECG Reconstruction from PPG Signals
authors: Xiaoyan Li; Shixin Xu; Faisal Habib; Neda Aminnejad; Arvind Gupta; Huaxiong Huang
model_family: GAN (CLEP-GAN: Attention U-Net generators + contrastive learning + dual time/frequency discriminators; CLEP-VQGAN variant with VQ-VAE)
task: PPG2ECG (subject-independent)
datasets: BIDMC PPG and Respiration; CapnoBase TBME RR (resampled 300->125 Hz); ODE-based synthetic ECG-PPG dataset (RSR, SA, AFib)
loss_functions: NT-Xent contrastive loss (PPG->ECG) + reconstruction losses Lp2p, Le2e, Lp2e + VQ dictionary & commitment losses (VQGAN variant) + adversarial losses from time-domain and STFT-spectrogram frequency-domain discriminators; Ltotal = 30·Lgen + 3·Lt + 1·Lf
loss_families: Adversarial (GAN); Spectral / frequency; Contrastive / CLIP; VQ / codebook
eval_metrics: RR-interval distribution: relative Histogram Intersection (rHI), relative RMSE, relative EMD, KL divergence, two-sample KS test; waveform RMSE; MAE of heart rate (MAE_HR); HRV (mean RR, SDNN of RR) GT vs reconstruction; Fréchet Distance in feature space; MFLOPs, MParams, inference time
metric_families: Efficiency (NFE / runtime / params); FID / embedding Fréchet; Heart rate / HRV; KL / JS divergence; RMSE; Subgroup performance gap; Visual inspection (qualitative)
eval_categories: Fidelity; Fairness; Robustness; Clinical validity; Efficiency
fairness: Examines influence of sex on reconstruction: sex-specific vs mixed-sex vs pretrain+finetune training on BIDMC male/female pairs; same-sex training yields better RMSE/MAE_HR; age and health conditions discussed as factors.
robustness: Subject-independent evaluation on held-out subjects; ablations (no contrastive/adversarial learning); λ sensitivity reported as robust; single-subject personalised experiments.
embedding_extractor: not specified (FD 'in feature space', following CardioGAN-type refs)
notes: RR-interval histogram metrics with fixed bin width used to validate the synthetic ODE dataset. Analyses effects of sex/age on reconstruction; warns against indiscriminate dataset augmentation. T-wave reconstruction remains inconsistent. Baselines: CardioGAN, QRS-ED, RDDM.
takeaway: RR-interval distribution comparison with several divergences (HI, EMD, KL, KS) is a simple rhythm-fidelity metric family worth adding.

title: Compact Latent Manifold Translation: A Parameter-Efficient Foundation Model for Cross-Modal and Cross-Frequency Physiological Signal Synthesis
authors: Bo Cui; Xiaowen Song; Yaowen Zhang; Shunzhe Zhang; B. J. F. van Beijnum; Monique Tabak; Ying Wang
model_family: Other (RVQ-VAE universal tokenizer + Transformer latent translator + latent masked-autoencoder; discrete-codebook foundation model)
task: PPG2ECG; super-resolution (25 Hz -> 100 Hz)
datasets: not reported (heterogeneous ECG/PPG datasets; names not found in text)
loss_functions: Stage 1: shape-aware reconstruction L1 + alpha*(1 - cosine similarity) + beta*L1 on temporal gradient (alpha=beta=0.5) + lambda_vq * VQ commitment loss; Stage 2: MSE latent distillation (translator and SR MAE)
loss_families: L1 reconstruction; L2 / MSE reconstruction; VQ / codebook
eval_metrics: RMSE; MAE; R-peak detection F1-score; Frechet Distance (FD); Pearson correlation; PSD-RMSE; UMAP latent visualization
metric_families: Curve Fréchet distance; Efficiency (NFE / runtime / params); Fiducial / R-peak timing; MAE; Pearson / correlation; RMSE; Spectral / PSD similarity; t-SNE / UMAP / PCA plots
notes: R-peak F1 used as a clinical landmark-preservation metric: 0.83 vs 0.37 baseline P2E; FD halved 37.49->16.18. SR: Pearson 0.9956, PSD-RMSE 0.0013, FD 0.0406. Argues MSE regression oversmooths QRS. 0.09B params (efficiency claim).
takeaway: R-peak detection F1 between real and generated signals is a simple landmark-fidelity metric; PSD-RMSE complements PSD JS divergence.

title: Complementarity-Preserving Generative Theory for Multimodal ECG Synthesis: A Quantum-Inspired Approach
authors: Timothy Oladunni; Farouk Ganiyu-Adewumi; Clyde Baidoo; Kyndal Maclin
model_family: GAN (quantum-inspired Q-CFD-GAN, complex-valued latent, Hermitian interference operator, tri-domain decoder)
task: unconditional (multimodal: time, STFT spectrum, time-frequency scalogram of beats)
datasets: multimodal ECG dataset from Mendeley Data (patient-level 70/15/15 split)
loss_functions: adversarial with gradient penalty + lambda1*CFD complementarity loss (tri-domain complementarity alignment + orthogonality penalty) + lambda2*interference-preserving loss + lambda3*physiological morphology loss (QRS and ST L2 terms)
loss_families: Adversarial (GAN); WGAN / gradient penalty; L2 / MSE reconstruction; Physiology / physics
eval_metrics: embedding variance and excess-variance ratio (pretrained multimodal encoder); classifier-based plausibility gap (KL divergence of pretrained classifier outputs real vs synthetic); tri-domain complementarity retention; RMS energy deviation (%); morphology contraction coefficient; peak-to-peak amplitude, RMS energy and spectral entropy distributions; RMS-P2P joint manifold
metric_families: KL / JS divergence; Other: amplitude/energy statistics; Other: cross-domain complementarity; Other: embedding variance ratio; Other: feature distribution plots
embedding_extractor: pretrained multimodal ECG encoder and pretrained ECG classifier (unspecified)
notes: Novel classifier-output KL 'plausibility gap' (0.157 vs 0.214 for MI-GAN) and cross-domain complementarity retention (0.91). Metrics derived from their own theory; single dataset; no TSTR or expert evaluation.
takeaway: Classifier-output KL plausibility gap and P2P/RMS/spectral-entropy distribution plots are easy additions.

title: Condition-fusion-and-hiding denoising diffusion model for electrocardiogram lead reconstruction
authors: Xiaoyang Wei; Zhiyuan Li; Yuanyuan Tian; Mengxiao Wang; Yanrui Jin; Weiping Ding; Chengliang Liu
model_family: Diffusion (CFH-DDPM: condition-fusion-and-hiding DDPM); baselines VAE, EKGAN, DDPM
task: lead-reconstruction
datasets: PTB-XL; CPSC2018
loss_functions: not reported
eval_metrics: Per-lead Sum of Squared Difference (SSD); Percentage Root-mean-square Difference (PRD %); Cosine Similarity (%); Signal-to-Noise Ratio (SNR dB)
metric_families: Cosine similarity; MSE; PRD / normalised PRD; PSNR / SNR
robustness: Evaluated on two datasets (PTB-XL and CPSC2018) with per-lead comparisons against VAE, EKGAN, DDPM baselines.
notes: Only supplementary tables available. CFH-DDPM mean PTB-XL: SSD 31.84, PRD 73.78%, COS 68.59%, SNR 4.79 dB; EKGAN has lower PRD (69.78%). Limb leads III/aVF show PRD >100% for all models, showing PRD saturates for poorly predictable leads.
takeaway: Report reconstruction metrics per lead: averages hide that some leads (III, aVF) are essentially unpredictable (PRD>100%).

title: Conditional Electrocardiogram Generation Using Hierarchical Variational Autoencoders
authors: Ivan Sviridov; Konstantin Egorov
model_family: VAE (hierarchical conditional Nouveau VAE, cNVAE-ECG; also 2D-cNVAE-ECG variant)
task: class-cond; augmentation
datasets: PTB-XL (training, binary MI vs SR and multi-label); Georgia and Ningbo (PhysioNet/CinC 2021) for transfer-learning downstream evaluation
loss_functions: NVAE ELBO: hierarchical KL terms + reconstruction likelihood modelled as mixture of discretized logistic distributions
loss_families: KL / ELBO
eval_metrics: downstream AUROC of XResNet1d101 classifier: binary (MI vs SR) and multi-label (LAD, LVH, AF, STach, IAVB, SB, TAb) with varying synthetic proportions; transfer learning (pretrain on synthetic/real, fine-tune on Georgia/Ningbo)
metric_families: Augmentation gain; Downstream classification
robustness: Downstream benefit evaluated on external Georgia and Ningbo datasets via transfer learning; results averaged over multiple synthetic proportions.
notes: Baselines: conditional WaveGAN* and Pulse2Pulse. AUROC gains up to ~2% (1.5% binary, 1.8% with MI addition). Evaluation is utility-only (augmentation ratios 0.1-2.0, pretraining); no distributional or morphology fidelity metrics. Percentile (2.5-97.5) amplitude filtering per lead.
takeaway: Augmentation-ratio sweeps and transfer-learning pretraining are useful utility protocols; complement with fidelity metrics.

title: Conditional generative adversarial network driven variable-duration single-lead to 12-lead electrocardiogram reconstruction
authors: Zehui Zhan; Jia‐Rong Chen; Kangming Li; Linfei Huang; Lin Xu; Gui‐Bin Bian; Richard Charles Millham; Victor Hugo C. de Albuquerque; Wanqing Wu
model_family: GAN (conditional LSGAN-style: ResNet 1D generator lead I -> 11 leads, small CNN discriminator; R-peak-aligned beat-wise generation stitched to variable length)
task: lead reconstruction (I→12)
datasets: CPSC2018 (6,877 12-lead recordings, 9 classes, 6-60 s; 80/20 patient-level split); ChinaDB / Chapman-Shaoxing (10,646 10-s 12-lead recordings) for validation
loss_functions: least-squares adversarial loss + lambda-weighted MSE reconstruction loss (generator); least-squares discriminator loss
loss_families: Adversarial (GAN); Least-squares / hinge GAN; L2 / MSE reconstruction
eval_metrics: Pearson correlation coefficient per lead and per class at beat level (mean 0.744) and segment level (mean 0.744; aVR 0.91, III 0.50); 9-class arrhythmia accuracy and macro-F1 with single-lead vs generated 12-lead vs real 12-lead (SENet classifier); per-class F1; confusion matrices; per-input-lead CC sweep; replicated baselines (LSTM&CNN, GAN of Seo et al., VAE-CNN) compared by CC; model parameters and runtime
metric_families: Downstream classification; Efficiency (NFE / runtime / params); Pearson / correlation; Visual inspection (qualitative)
eval_categories: Fidelity; Utility; Robustness; Clinical validity; Efficiency
robustness: Cross-dataset check: model compared on ChinaDB in addition to CPSC2018 (CC 0.72).
notes: Accuracy/macro-F1: lead I 0.71/0.66, generated 12-lead 0.74/0.70, real 12-lead 0.81/0.77; CC vs baselines 0.74 (CPSC) / 0.72 (ChinaDB) vs Seo GAN 0.73/0.72, VAE-CNN 0.60/0.64. Only paired CC is used for fidelity (no amplitude error, no Einthoven/Goldberger consistency check even though limb leads are linearly determined by two leads); the 'generated 12-lead' classifier takes the max over separate lead-I, limb, chest and 12-lead classifiers, so part of the gain may come from ensembling.
takeaway: For lead-reconstruction tasks ECGEN-Eval should report paired per-lead correlation and amplitude error together with an inter-lead (Einthoven/Goldberger) consistency check and a classifier-based diagnostic-gap metric (single-lead vs generated vs real 12-lead), keeping the classifier fixed to avoid ensemble confounds.

title: Cross-Lead Attention Transformers with GAN Oversampling for Robust ECG Arrhythmia Detection
authors: Ahmed Tibermacine; Imad Eddine Tibermacine; M’hamed Mancer; Ilyes Naidji; Lahcene Mamen; Abdelaziz Rabehi; Mustapha Habib
model_family: GAN (standard vanilla GAN, BCE loss, latent dim 100, beat-level oversampling) + per-lead CNN / cross-lead Transformer classifier
task: class-cond augmentation (minority arrhythmia beat oversampling, per-class GAN)
datasets: MIT-BIH Arrhythmia (16 classes, 2 leads, patient-level 60/15/25 split); external: ECG5000 (single-lead, 140 points), St Petersburg INCART (12-lead, resampled to 360 Hz)
loss_functions: standard minimax GAN binary cross-entropy (classifier: cross-entropy)
loss_families: Adversarial (GAN); Classification CE
eval_metrics: DTW distance; Pearson correlation; MMD; SNR (dB); intra-class variance ratio (synthetic/real); blinded expert real-vs-synthetic identification (2 cardiologists, 200+200 beats); diagnostic consistency; physiological plausibility score (1-5); augmentation gain in rare-class F1 (real-only vs augmented); accuracy/precision/recall/F1/AUC; model size/FLOPs/latency after pruning/INT8
metric_families: Augmentation gain; Cross-dataset / external validation; DTW; Diversity / mode-collapse measure; Efficiency (NFE / runtime / params); Expert / Turing test; Expert diagnostic agreement; MMD; PSNR / SNR; Pearson / correlation
eval_categories: Fidelity; Diversity; Utility; Robustness; Human / expert; Conditional consistency; Efficiency
robustness: Classifier externally validated on ECG5000 and INCART; generator robustness not studied.
notes: 5,000 synthetic beats (1,000 each IVR, VFL, AFL, SVTA, aberrated APB): DTW 0.31±0.12, Pearson 0.84±0.09, MMD 0.042, SNR 23.7 dB, variance ratio 0.88-1.12; cardiologists identified synthetic beats at 47.8% (chance), diagnostic consistency 91.5%, plausibility 4.1/5; augmentation +0.8-1.5 F1 pts on rare classes. Pairing for DTW/correlation and the MMD kernel/feature space are not described, and ablation (macro F1 94.75% without augmentation) is inconsistent with Table 11 (+1.2 pts); 99.67% accuracy suspiciously high for 16-class inter-patient MIT-BIH.
takeaway: Good template for a multi-angle report (similarity + variance-ratio diversity + expert + utility); ECGEN-Eval should add a per-class synthetic/real variance-ratio diversity metric and require explicit pairing and kernel/feature documentation for DTW/correlation/MMD so such numbers are reproducible.

title: Data imbalance in cardiac health diagnostics using CECG-GAN
authors: Yang Y, Lan T, Wang Y, Li F, Liu L, Huang X, Gao F, Jiang S, Zhang Z, Chen X.
model_family: GAN (conditional, TimeGAN-style with Transformer encoder/decoder/generator/discriminator; 'CECG-GAN')
task: class-cond / augmentation (imbalanced arrhythmia)
datasets: MIT-BIH Arrhythmia; CPSC2020
loss_functions: Adversarial (conditional GAN) loss + TimeGAN-style embedding/recovery reconstruction and supervised latent-matching loss (details not formally given)
loss_families: Adversarial (GAN)
eval_metrics: PRD; Fréchet Distance (discrete, per-pair); RMSE; MAE; downstream classifier Precision, Recall, F1, Accuracy; per-patient evaluation; comparison to BiLSTM-CNN GAN, LSTM-AE GAN, LSTM-VAE GAN, SimGAN
metric_families: Augmentation gain; Curve Fréchet distance; MAE; PRD / normalised PRD; RMSE
notes: Abstract reports PRD 55.048 (high, yet claimed 'high similarity'), FD 1.139, RMSE 0.232, MAE 0.166; best patient PRD 21.1. Synthetic samples filtered by whether they improve classifier F1 - risk of selection bias/leakage. FD is pairwise discrete Fréchet, not FID-style.
takeaway: Clarify FD naming (discrete Fréchet vs Fréchet-Gaussian) and warn against classifier-guided sample selection in utility evaluation.

title: Deep conditional generative model for personalization of 12-lead electrocardiograms and cardiovascular risk prediction
authors: Sang Y, Banerjee A, Beetz M, Grau V.
model_family: VAE (conditional VAE, 1D conv encoder/decoder) + Cox proportional-hazards head
task: other (personalised generation conditioned on demographics, heart pose, electrode positions; CVD risk prediction)
conditioning: Patient attributes (age, sex, ...); Physiological parameters / simulator
datasets: UK Biobank (37,508 volunteers; 21,083 with ECG+MRI; 1,834 with electrode positions); in silico simulations (Mincholé et al.)
loss_functions: cVAE ELBO: MSE reconstruction + KL divergence; plus Cox partial-likelihood survival loss; Ltotal = Lrecons + LKL + Lsurv (equal weights)
loss_families: L2 / MSE reconstruction; KL / ELBO
eval_metrics: qualitative comparison of morphology trends (R/S/T amplitudes per lead) against in silico simulation under heart rotation/translation; C-index for CVD risk; Kaplan-Meier stratification
metric_families: Downstream classification; Other: comparison to biophysical simulation; Statistical tests
notes: No quantitative generative-quality metric; validation is lead-wise agreement of amplitude trends with biophysical simulation (often only partially agrees). C-index 0.63-0.65 from latent embeddings.
takeaway: Simulation-consistency (controllability: does changing a condition shift morphology as physics predicts) is a distinct evaluation axis.

title: Deep Generative Models: The winning key for large and easily accessible ECG datasets?
authors: Giuliana Monachino; Beatrice Zanchi; Luigi Fiorillo; Giulio Conte; Angelo Auricchio; Athina Tzovara; Francesca Dalia Faraci
model_family: Survey/EvalOnly (narrative review of VAE, GAN, diffusion and hybrid/physiology-constrained DGMs for ECG)
task: survey (ECG data scarcity, augmentation and anonymisation via DGMs)
datasets: reviewed: MIT-BIH Arrhythmia, PTB, CinC2017, VFDB, CUDB, PTB-XL and others (no experiments)
loss_functions: not applicable
eval_metrics: catalogued: visual inspection; cardiologist real-vs-fake test; external real-vs-fake classifier; distribution metrics (MMD, relative entropy, EMD, statistics of ECG feature distributions e.g. RR/QT/R-amplitude/QRS axis, t-SNE); pairwise metrics (Euclidean distance, MAE, SSIM, MSE-based, DTW/time-warping, Fréchet distance, Chamfer distance, template comparison); downstream classifier gain; membership inference attack; identity verificator accuracy
metric_families: Augmentation gain; Classifier two-sample test; Clinical intervals (PR/QRS/QT/ST); Curve Fréchet distance; DTW; Euclidean distance; Expert / Turing test; KL / JS divergence; MAE; MMD; MSE; Membership inference / re-identification; Other: Chamfer distance; SSIM; Signal quality index; Visual inspection (qualitative); Wasserstein / EMD; t-SNE / UMAP / PCA plots
eval_categories: Fidelity; Utility; Privacy; Fairness; Clinical validity; Human / expert
fairness: Discusses single-centre data collection causing demographic/geographic bias and class imbalance, but proposes no fairness metric.
privacy: Central theme: ECG is a biometric so removing PHI is insufficient; DGMs proposed for anonymisation, but only 3 works assess privacy (membership inference, identity verificator) and a robust anonymisation metric is lacking.
notes: Groups evaluation into fidelity, classification effectiveness and anonymisation; splits fidelity metrics into distribution-level (MMD, RE, EMD, feature statistics, t-SNE) and pairwise time-ordered (ED, MAE, SSIM, MSE, DTW, FD, Chamfer) metrics. Concludes there is no consensus or reference thresholds, metrics are implemented inconsistently, utility metrics are task/classifier-dependent, and only 3 anonymisation works evaluate privacy (2 via membership inference); recommends a standardised multi-perspective metric set (morphology, rhythm, noise) mimicking clinician inspection.
takeaway: Use its distribution-level vs pairwise split to organise the report, add a Chamfer distance and real-template comparison, and always print real-vs-real reference values so that users have the 'realistic enough' thresholds the review says are missing.

title: Deep Learning Driven Physiological Signal Generation: An Improved DDIM-Based ECG Synthesis Framework
authors: Yuchen Wang; Yixue Li; Yongjian Li; Yiheng Sun; Meng Chen; Shoushui Wei
venue: International Congress on Image and Signal Processing, BioMedical Engineering and Informatics (CISP-BMEI)
model_family: Diffusion (DDIM 'AD-DIM/ECG-DDIM' with ShiftNet structure-aware forward encoder, shifted diffusion offset, lightweight MSCnet/BConv reverse network, 0.08 M params)
task: class-specific augmentation (AF vs normal, class-imbalanced AF detection)
datasets: MIT-BIH AFDB; SPHDB (private 24 h wearable paroxysmal-AF recordings, 250 patients, Shandong Provincial Hospital); CPSC2018; PTB-XL
loss_functions: diffusion denoising objective with SNR-modulated implicit optimisation (not formally specified); classifier trained with cross-entropy
loss_families: Diffusion noise prediction; Classification CE
eval_metrics: downstream classification Acc/Sen/Spe/F1 (CGLNet) after balancing with generated AF at 5:1/3:1/1:1 ratios; Acc/F1 vs forward noise intensity; DTW to random real templates (figure only); parameters and GFLOPs vs GAN, VAE-CNN, E-LSTM, DDIM; qualitative P/T-wave comparison; conclusion also claims SNR gain, SSIM > 0.92, FID-ECG 12.7, 42% DTW reduction, 0.3 s/sample without reported experiments
metric_families: Augmentation gain; DTW; Downstream classification; Efficiency (NFE / runtime / params); Visual inspection (qualitative)
notes: With 1:1 balancing, AFDB Acc/F1 99.49/99.48, CPSC2018 97.84/98.10, PTB-XL 92.36/91.89; vs augmentation baselines Acc/F1 98.15/98.22 (DDIM 97.34/97.52, GAN 91.16/91.34) with 0.08 M params. Paper is internally inconsistent: conclusion reports metrics (SSIM, FID-ECG, SNR, 'MIT-BIH' experiments, 43%/42% distortion reductions) absent from the results, DTW results are only a figure, and the P/T-wave comparison replaces non-target segments with the original ECG, so it is a paired local error; low-confidence evidence.
takeaway: Segment-wise (P-wave / T-wave window) fidelity is a useful idea for the clinical feature extractor, but this paper shows why ECGEN-Eval reports must state pairing, sample counts and embedding network for every number, since unsupported headline metrics (FID-ECG, SSIM) cannot be reproduced.

title: DiffECG: A Versatile Probabilistic Diffusion Model for ECG Signals Synthesis
authors: Nour Neifar; Achraf Ben Hamadou; Afef Mdhaffar; Mohamed Jmaïel
venue: IEEE/ACIS International Conference on Software Engineering Research, Management and Applications (SERA)
model_family: Diffusion (DDPM on spectrograms, conditional U-Net; DiffECG)
task: class-cond generation; imputation; forecasting (heartbeat-level)
datasets: MIT-BIH Arrhythmia (MLII lead; classes N, V, F)
loss_functions: DDPM noise-prediction (epsilon) loss + MSE regression loss between generated and ground-truth signal (imputation/forecasting)
loss_families: L2 / MSE reconstruction; Diffusion noise prediction
eval_metrics: RMSE; MAE; FID; DTW; Earth Mover's Distance (EMD); MMD; downstream arrhythmia classifier Accuracy, Precision, Recall, F1 (train real + synthetic); visual inspection
metric_families: Augmentation gain; DTW; FID / embedding Fréchet; MAE; MMD; RMSE; Wasserstein / EMD
notes: Per-class (N, V, F) metric tables; FID values ~1e-3 indicate non-standard FID computation (not Inception-based on images). 70/30 signal-wise split. Augmentation compared against 4 GAN baselines with 3 classifiers. Qualitative check only by authors.
takeaway: EMD and per-class reporting are cheap additions; FID without a specified extractor is not comparable across papers.

title: DiffuSETS: 12-lead ECG Generation Conditioned on Clinical Text Reports and Patient-Specific Information
authors: Yongfan Lai; Jiabo Chen; Deyun Zhang; Yue Wang; Shijia Geng; Hongyan Li; Shenda Hong
model_family: Diffusion (latent DDPM U-Net with cross-attention on LLM text embeddings + patient info; VAE latent space)
task: text-cond
datasets: MIMIC-IV-ECG (+ MIMIC-IV-Clinical for age/sex); PTB-XL (external)
loss_functions: Latent DDPM noise-prediction MSE ||ε-ε̂(z_t,t,c)||²; VAE: MSE reconstruction + λ·KL divergence
loss_families: L2 / MSE reconstruction; Diffusion noise prediction; KL / ELBO
eval_metrics: Signal level: FID; improved precision/recall/F1 (Kynkäänniemi manifold) on embeddings; Feature level: heart-rate MAE (conditioned vs generated HR); Diagnostic level: CLIP score (text-ECG alignment); clinical Turing test (2 cardiologists, 50 real+50 generated); expert semantic-alignment check (100 ECGs, 76%); heart-age correlation via AnyECG (r=0.594); downstream augmentation classification for rare classes
metric_families: Augmentation gain; Demographic attribute preservation; Expert / Turing test; Expert diagnostic agreement; FID / embedding Fréchet; Label / condition adherence; Precision / recall / density / coverage; Text–ECG alignment (CLIP)
eval_categories: Fidelity; Diversity; Utility; Fairness; Robustness; Clinical validity; Human / expert; Conditional consistency
fairness: Age conditioning checked indirectly via heart-age correlation of generated ECGs; authors note sex/age are hard to quantify and use heart rate instead. No subgroup performance analysis.
robustness: External validation on PTB-XL in addition to internal MIMIC-IV-ECG evaluation.
embedding_extractor: pretrained Net1D ECG encoder (FID, P/R); Net1D + text encoder CLIP-style model for CLIP score
notes: Proposes three-level benchmark (signal/feature/diagnostic). Argues MAE unreliable due to phase shifts, uses manifold P/R instead. MIMIC: FID 23.6, F1 0.894, HR-MAE 4.15, CLIP 0.812. Baselines WaveGAN, Pulse2Pulse, SSSD-ECG on PTB-XL.
takeaway: Adopt three-level protocol: embedding FID + manifold precision/recall, condition-adherence MAE (e.g., HR), and text/label alignment via a CLIP-style ECG-text encoder.

title: Diffusion Model-Based Multi-scale Feature and Timing Consistency Enhancement for ECG Signal Generation
authors: Yuan Wang; Yu Weng; Wengjian Liu
venue: Lecture Notes in Computer Science (KSEM 2025, LNAI 15919)
model_family: Diffusion (DDPM, 1000 steps; dilated-conv UNet with db4 3-level wavelet sub-band branches, pyramid pooling and 4-head lightweight Transformer bottleneck)
task: unconditional (augmentation)
datasets: MIT-BIH Arrhythmia (MLII/V1, 34 train / 14 test records); PTB Diagnostic ECG Database (lead II, 80/20)
loss_functions: DDPM noise MSE + 0.5 x DTW alignment loss to real signals + 0.3 x wavelet-domain multi-scale matching loss
loss_families: L2 / MSE reconstruction; Diffusion noise prediction; Spectral / frequency; DTW loss
eval_metrics: MSE; SNR (defined, not reported); Fréchet distance (feature space unspecified); sample variance (diversity); 3-cardiologist blinded expert score 1-5; QRS duration error; P-onset/QRS-onset/T-end time deviation; RR-interval SD; DTW distance; ResNet-1D arrhythmia classification accuracy (MIT-BIH) and F1 (PTB) with real+synthetic training; params/training/inference time; two-sample t-tests
metric_families: Augmentation gain; Clinical intervals (PR/QRS/QT/ST); DTW; Diversity / mode-collapse measure; Efficiency (NFE / runtime / params); Expert / Turing test; FID / embedding Fréchet; Heart rate / HRV; MSE; Statistical tests
eval_categories: Fidelity; Diversity; Utility; Clinical validity; Human / expert; Efficiency
notes: Proposed vs single-scale DDPM: MSE 0.032 vs 0.041, FD 24.6 vs 28.3, variance 0.18 vs 0.15, expert 4.2 vs 3.5; RR SD 13.3 ms (real 12.5, DDPM 27.8); DTW 17.3 vs 35.7; QRS duration error 8 ms; augmentation ACC 92.3→95.6% (MIT-BIH), F1 0.87→0.91 (PTB); 14.2 M params, 20 ms/sample. Caveats: MSE/DTW/waveform deviations for an unconditional model with no stated pairing; FD feature space not defined; 'Variance' used as diversity; reference list contains errors (GaN semiconductor paper cited for GAN), so reported numbers should be treated cautiously.
takeaway: The RR-interval-variability and fiducial-timing comparisons are what ECGEN-Eval's hrv metric and feature extractor already provide; ECGEN-Eval should require that any FD report names its feature space (fd handcrafted vs fed backbone) and that paired metrics state the pairing rule.

title: Disentangled conditional generation of ECG signals with interpretable latent factors
authors: Rong Xiao; Zhijun Xiao; Jianqing Li; Chengyu Liu
venue: Computer Methods and Programs in Biomedicine
model_family: Hybrid VAE + normalizing flow (Transformer beta-TC-VAE with attention pooling, 8-d latent + RealNVP-style class-conditional latent flow used only at generation)
task: class-cond (5 PTB-XL superclasses; out-of-domain MIT-BIH NORM/LBBB/RBBB/PVC via flow fine-tuning) + interpretable/disentangled generation
datasets: PTB-XL (lead I; folds 1-8 train, 9 test, 10 eval); ECGSYN simulator data (training + factor ground truth); MIT-BIH Arrhythmia (out-of-domain only); PTB-XL+ ECGdeli features (post-hoc)
loss_functions: beta-TCVAE objective (reconstruction + alpha*index-code MI + beta*total correlation + gamma*dimension-wise KL; alpha=1.2, beta=2, gamma=0.6); flow: MMD between flow samples and class posterior latents + conditional NLL
loss_families: KL / ELBO; Token cross-entropy
eval_metrics: MIG (proxy factors from NeuroKit2 on real ECG; ground-truth ECGSYN factors); SAP; R² latent-factor decodability; Jacobian sensitivity; latent traversals; Fake-Test (train-real/test-synthetic RBF-SVM accuracy, 'fidelity'); Fake-Train (train-synthetic/test-real, 'diversity'); signal-level distribution projections; class-mean waveforms; augmentation accuracy (1D-CNN); Spearman correlation of latent with ECGdeli ST elevation
metric_families: Augmentation gain; Cross-dataset / external validation; Other: disentanglement (MIG/SAP); R² (coefficient of determination); Statistical tests; TSTR / TRTS; Visual inspection (qualitative); t-SNE / UMAP / PCA plots
eval_categories: Fidelity; Diversity; Utility; Robustness; Clinical validity; Conditional consistency
robustness: Out-of-domain evaluation on MIT-BIH with frozen PTB-XL backbone and recording/patient-disjoint split; disentanglement factor correspondence partially retained.
notes: Proxy MIG 0.53 (ECGSYN MIG 0.27); in-domain Fake-Test/Fake-Train 44.4%/45.3% with flow vs 20.0%/17.9% prior sampling (5-class chance 20%); out-of-domain 66.3%/80.1% vs 33.4%/32.2%; SSSD-ECG released samples 48.6/47.0, retrained Pulse2Pulse-style WaveGAN* 28.5/28.8 under the same protocol. Augmentation gains tiny (73.07 -> 73.70%). Classifier-based TRTS/TSTR accuracies are the only generative metrics; demonstrates prior-sampling collapse that reconstruction metrics would miss.
takeaway: Add a classifier-based TRTS/TSTR (Fake-Test/Fake-Train) conditional metric with explicit chance level, since it exposed prior-sampling mode collapse to class-average beats that per-sample fidelity metrics would not flag.

title: Disentangling Physiology from Fidelity: Latent-Guided Diffusion Models for Cross-Modal Cardiac Synthesis
authors: Chenyang Xu; Siming Li; Wensai Xuan; Hao Wang
venue: IEEE International Conference on Acoustics Speech and Signal Processing
model_family: Hybrid (shared Mamba-VAE encoder -> latent code z + metadata guiding a conditional Mamba U-Net diffusion decoder with AdaLN, 'Mamba-Diff-VAE', 100 steps)
task: cross-modal translation ECG<->PCG (bidirectional) with metadata (rest/post-exercise) conditioning
conditioning: Other signal (SCG, BCG, radar, video, ...); Physiological parameters / simulator
datasets: EPHNOGRAM (69 subjects, 15,847 paired 10 s segments, subject-disjoint 80/10/10 split)
loss_functions: epsilon-MSE diffusion loss + beta=0.05 KL divergence on VAE latent
loss_families: L2 / MSE reconstruction; Diffusion noise prediction; KL / ELBO
eval_metrics: MSE; Pearson correlation; heart-rate MAE (ECG->PCG, BPM); R-peak MAE (PCG->ECG); QRS-S1 interval MAE (ms); 1D FID with PhysioNet 2016 pretrained 1D ResNet; inference time (ms/segment); t-SNE of latent space; qualitative waveform/spectrogram plots; 5 seeds mean +/- std
metric_families: Efficiency (NFE / runtime / params); FID / embedding Fréchet; Fiducial / R-peak timing; Heart rate / HRV; MSE; Pearson / correlation; Visual inspection (qualitative); t-SNE / UMAP / PCA plots
eval_categories: Fidelity; Clinical validity; Conditional consistency; Efficiency
embedding_extractor: 1D ResNet pretrained on PhysioNet/CinC Challenge 2016 (heart-sound classification) for FID
notes: PCG->ECG: MSE 0.112, Corr 0.821, R-peak MAE 1.35, FID 18.2 vs best baseline SSSD-style diffusion 0.173 / 0.738 / 2.19 / 29.8; ECG->PCG: MSE 0.089, Corr 0.847, HR MAE 1.15 BPM, FID 16.5, QRS-S1 MAE 12.4 ms. Paired metrics vs ground truth are appropriate for translation, but FID for generated ECG uses a PCG-challenge feature extractor and FID has no std; 69 healthy subjects only, no pathology.
takeaway: For paired cross-modal translation, add R-peak timing MAE and heart-rate MAE between generated and ground-truth ECG to the clinical metrics, and warn when FID/FED is computed with an encoder trained on a different modality (here a PCG network) rather than an ECG backbone.

title: DiSR-ECG: Residual Shifting Conditional Diffusion for Robust ECG Super-Resolution
authors: Fan-Yi Hsu; I Chiu; Kuan-Chen Wang; Sheng-Yu Peng; Yu Tsao
model_family: Diffusion (residual-shifting conditional diffusion, ResShift-style, Mamba temporal backbone; DiSR-ECG)
task: super-resolution (50 Hz -> 500 Hz, with noise robustness)
datasets: PTB-XL (train/in-domain); Chapman-Shaoxing (zero-shot cross-dataset); MIT-BIH Noise Stress Test DB (noise injection)

loss_families: L1 reconstruction
eval_metrics: MSE; Cosine Similarity (CoS); SNR (dB); Maximum Absolute Deviation (MAD); paired-sample t-test significance
metric_families: Cosine similarity; Cross-dataset / external validation; MSE; Noise / perturbation robustness; Other: maximum absolute deviation; PSNR / SNR; Statistical tests
robustness: Noisy inputs via MIT-BIH NSTDB contaminants (bw/em/ma) at varied SNRs; zero-shot cross-dataset evaluation on Chapman-Shaoxing; paired t-tests for significance.
notes: 15 diffusion steps; 10-sample ensemble at inference. Baselines: linear interpolation, SRECG, DCAE-SR, MSECG. Significance testing (p<0.05) of improvements is a good practice. Ablation: removing SI-SDR lowers SNR. Cross-dataset generalization emphasised.
takeaway: Add SI-SDR / cosine similarity / max-abs-deviation for paired tasks, plus paired significance tests.

title: DS4U-Net: A Diffusion Model-Based Approach to Multi-Lead ECG Signal Generation
authors: Tiantian Du; Jiwei Wang; Rui Qu; Zhe Zhu
venue: International Conference on Intelligent Computing and Signal Processing (ICSP)
model_family: Diffusion (DDPM, T=200, S4 layers fused into 1D U-Net denoiser; same network also used for a learned forward noising process)
task: class-cond (12-lead ECG generation for data augmentation, category-code conditioning)
datasets: PTB-XL
loss_functions: MSE noise-prediction (epsilon) loss
loss_families: L2 / MSE reconstruction; Diffusion noise prediction
eval_metrics: visual inspection (beats and 12-lead plots); qualitative spectral comparison; MSE; RMSE; MAE; MAPE; DTW; Euclidean distance (per lead I/II/III, 3000 random synthetic signals); SE-ResNet classification AUC and accuracy on real data (TSTR); ablation by classification
metric_families: DTW; Euclidean distance; MAE; MSE; Other: MAPE; RMSE; TSTR / TRTS; Visual inspection (qualitative)
notes: Lead I: MSE 0.035, RMSE 0.187, MAE 0.109, DTW 47.6, ED 3.83 vs best GAN baseline (WaveGAN, Pulse2Pulse, SeqGAN, TimeGAN) MSE 0.043; SE-ResNet AUC 0.834 / acc 0.878 vs Pulse2Pulse 0.791/0.802. Pairwise MSE/DTW/ED computed between randomly selected synthetic and real signals without any stated pairing scheme, so differences are small and hard to interpret; the abstract's 'spectral similarity' claim is only visual (no PSD metric).
takeaway: Illustrates the common misuse of paired metrics (MSE/DTW/ED) on unpaired class-conditional output; ECGEN-Eval's nearest-neighbour mae/dtw/prd and distributional psd should be documented as the correct replacements, with the pairing mode printed in the report.

title: ECG Generation Based on Denoising Diffusion Probabilistic Models
authors: Zhongyu Wang; Caiyun Ma; Minghui Zhao; Shuo Zhang; Jianqing Li; Chengyu Liu
model_family: Diffusion (DDPM, Attention U-Net; signal-, STFT-spectrogram- (Griffin-Lim) and wavelet-subband variants)
task: class-cond / augmentation (beats N, LBBB, RBBB, PVC)

loss_functions: DDPM noise-prediction L2 (epsilon MSE)
loss_families: L2 / MSE reconstruction; Diffusion noise prediction
eval_metrics: DTW; Euclidean distance (ED); Pearson correlation coefficient (PCC); KL divergence (KLD) - all between average synthetic beat and average real beat; visual inspection
metric_families: DTW; Euclidean distance; KL / JS divergence; Pearson / correlation; Visual inspection (qualitative)
notes: Metrics computed on class-mean templates only, so diversity/mode collapse is invisible. Best: ED 4.37, DTW 17.09 (direct signal diffusion); PCC 0.972, KLD 0.0094 (wavelet diffusion).
takeaway: Template (mean-beat) PCC/DTW is a useful cheap fidelity check but must be paired with diversity metrics.

title: ECG Monitor Design: From One to Three - Advancing ECG Monitoring with AI-Generated Lead Synthesis (GANs)
authors: Oumaima Chehaibi; Nesrine Majdoub; Taoufik Ladhari; Salim Hadj Saïd
venue: IEEE International Conference on Artificial Intelligence & Green Energy (ICAIGE)
model_family: GAN (conv encoder-decoder generator with latent + noise + optional class label; conv encoder discriminator pre-trained following Fawaz et al.)
task: lead reconstruction (I→II, III) for a reduced-electrode 3-lead hardware monitor
