embedding_extractor: pretrained xResNet1d classifiers from PulseImpute (downstream only)
notes: Follows PulseImpute benchmark. Transient 30%: PulseDiff-SSSDS4 MSE 0.0021; extended: 0.0192, deterministic BDC transformer still best. Notes diffusion trained on noise-space loss underperforms on long gaps.
takeaway: Beat-detection F1 with tolerance window and pretrained-classifier AUC on generated signals are reusable checks.

title: Introducing a Comprehensive Framework for Synthetic ECG Validation
authors: Zanchi B, Monachino G, Metaldi M, Conte G, Meystre S, Faraci FD.
venue: IEEE open journal of engineering in medicine and biology
model_family: EvalOnly (validation framework; applied to Pulse2Pulse GAN Brugada ECGs)
task: evaluation
datasets: Private Brugada type-I 12-lead ECGs (21 patients, 1122 10-s windows with 50% overlap) vs 1122 synthetic
loss_functions: n/a (Pulse2Pulse WGAN-GP referenced)
loss_families: WGAN / gradient penalty
eval_metrics: Four layers: (1) visual inspection; (2) morphology via NeuroKit on lead II: RR, PR, QRS, QT, QTc (Bazett), P/QRS/T axes, Mann-Whitney U; (3) similarity: Euclidean distance, maximum absolute error, cosine similarity, MSE, RMSE, NRMSE, RMSPE, kernel MMD, KL divergence, DTW (KMMD/KL/DTW on II, V1, V2) benchmarked against R-vs-R intra-subject and inter-subject distances; (4) expert cardiologist scoring
metric_families: Clinical intervals (PR/QRS/QT/ST); Cosine similarity; DTW; Expert / Turing test; Inter-lead consistency; KL / JS divergence; MMD; RMSE; Statistical tests; Visual inspection (qualitative)
notes: Only supplementary text available. Key idea: synthetic-to-real distance should lie between real intra-subject and inter-subject variability (R-vs-R benchmarking). Careful statistics: patient-level median aggregation to respect independence. Mentions EU AI Act/GMLP as validation gate.
takeaway: Adopt R-vs-R reference bands: express every distance metric relative to real intra-subject and inter-subject baselines.

title: Invertible Conditional Generative Adversarial Networks to Effectively Generate Myocardial Infarction from Normal ECG
authors: Sara Battiston; Roberto Sassi; Massimo Walter Rivolta
venue: 2025 47th Annual International Conference of the IEEE Engineering in Medicine and Biology Society (EMBC)
model_family: GAN (Invertible conditional GAN, IcGAN: 2D-conv cGAN + encoder mapping real beat to (z, y); compared with CycleGAN of equal generator size)
task: class-to-class style transfer of 12-lead heartbeats (NORM ↔ ASMI ↔ IMI)
conditioning: Class / diagnosis label; Other ECG leads
datasets: PTB-XL subset (10,776 ECGs: NORM, ASMI, IMI; 100 Hz; 35,353 beats, patient-wise 70/30 split)
loss_functions: cGAN adversarial (BCE, sigmoid discriminator); encoder trained with L2 loss to recover (z, y) from 3,000 generated beats; CycleGAN baseline with cycle-consistency
loss_families: Adversarial (GAN); L2 / MSE reconstruction; Cycle consistency
eval_metrics: 90% per-lead confidence bands (2,500 real vs synthetic); 2D UMAP density heatmap of real with synthetic overlay; GAN-train and GAN-test accuracy (ResNet-style CNN, 3 classes); per-lead ST-segment (80 ms) mean amplitude comparison with modified Hotelling T² simultaneous 95% CIs
metric_families: Clinical intervals (PR/QRS/QT/ST); Statistical tests; TSTR / TRTS; Visual inspection (qualitative); t-SNE / UMAP / PCA plots
eval_categories: Fidelity; Diversity; Utility; Clinical validity; Conditional consistency
notes: IcGAN GAN-test 84% (baseline 90%), GAN-train 73% (baseline 100%) vs CycleGAN 74%/60%, i.e. synthetic data form a narrower sub-distribution; ST-amplitude CIs include zero in 4/12 leads (synthetic ASMI) and 2/12 (synthetic NORM), mean differences −0.014 to 0.050 mV, below the 0.1 mV STEMI threshold. Evaluation is unpaired/distributional on transferred test beats; GAN-train/test baselines and splits differ (synthetic 21,212 vs real 10,606), no expert review, and no check that patient-specific features are preserved beyond visual examples.
takeaway: Add a per-lead clinical-feature comparison with simultaneous confidence intervals (e.g. ST amplitude from the features module) judged against clinical decision thresholds, and support GAN-train/GAN-test as a paired diversity/fidelity utility metric.

title: Investigating Transformer-Based GANs for Realistic ECG Time-Series Data Generation
authors: Gabriel B. Moro; Joaquim Assunção; Isabel Cristina Reinheimer; Carlos Eduardo Poli‐de‐Figueiredo; Luís A. L. Silva
venue: IEEE International Symposium on Computer-Based Medical Systems (CBMS)
model_family: GAN (TTS-CGAN: Transformer-encoder generator, ViT-style patch-embedding Transformer discriminator with adversarial + class heads; LSGAN loss, DiffAug, EMA)
task: class-cond (MIT-BIH 5 beat classes; MIMIC-IV heart-rate trend classes low/normal/high) + retraining the GAN on hybrid real/synthetic sets
datasets: MIT-BIH Arrhythmia (pre-processed 187-sample heartbeat version); MIMIC-IV (hourly charted heart-rate values, not ECG waveforms)
loss_functions: Least-squares GAN loss for G and D, plus discriminator class-classification head
loss_families: Adversarial (GAN); Least-squares / hinge GAN
eval_metrics: DTW on example real/synthetic pairs; PCA and t-SNE plots; mean cosine similarity; Jensen-Shannon distance (per class); heatmap visual comparison; same metrics after retraining the GAN on hybrid datasets with 20/40/60/100% synthetic
metric_families: Cosine similarity; DTW; KL / JS divergence; Other: recursive training on synthetic; Visual inspection (qualitative); t-SNE / UMAP / PCA plots
robustness: Retrains the generator on increasing fractions of its own synthetic output (up to 100%) and reports that cosine/JS stay stable but rare-class extremes are lost (model-collapse-style check).
notes: Cosine similarity 0.84 (non-ectopic) to 0.99 (MIMIC-IV HR classes), JS distance 0.12-0.24; example-pair DTW 0.17-0.26 (MIT-BIH) and 0.10-0.13 (MIMIC-IV). Despite the abstract, the 'hybrid' experiment retrains the GAN itself on mixed data and re-measures cosine/JS (up to 60% synthetic keeps metrics stable); no downstream classifier is trained. MIMIC-IV part models hourly heart-rate trends, not ECG; exact cosine/JS construction is not specified.
takeaway: Mean cosine similarity and value-histogram JS saturate near 1/0 on normalised beats; ECGEN-Eval should prefer embedding/feature-level distribution metrics (fd, mmd, pr_dist) and document that per-sample cosine on min-max normalised beats is not discriminative.

title: L2L-ESN: A Lead-to-Lead Electrocardiogram Synthesis Network for Assisting Myocardial Infarction Diagnosis
authors: Jian Tan; Xinrui Qiu; Zhanshuo Shang; Xunhua Huang; Haoyi Fan; Zongmin Wang
model_family: GAN (conditional WGAN-GP; 1D U-Net multihead generator with one output channel per target lead; 1D CNN critic on concatenated source+target leads)
task: lead reconstruction (II→7 key leads '1T7'; II+V1→6 key leads '2T6'; remaining 4 limb leads derived) + MI detection/localisation
datasets: PTB-XL (5486 MI: 3078 AMI, 3271 IMI); HeMI (private, Zhengzhou University; 26602 MI records: 8190 AMI, 9157 IMI)
loss_functions: conditional Wasserstein adversarial loss with gradient penalty (lambda_GP 10, n_critic 5) + MSE reconstruction (lambda_MSE:lambda_CWGAN = 50:1)
loss_families: Adversarial (GAN); WGAN / gradient penalty; L2 / MSE reconstruction
eval_metrics: RMSE; Pearson correlation (PCC); discrete curve Fréchet distance (FD) (mean±SD, MI vs non-MI); per-lead binary MI detection precision/recall/F1 using synthesized vs real lead; MI detection with limited real + synthetic lead combinations; AMI/IMI localisation P/R/F1; baselines SSSD-S4, ecg_recon, lead_recon with training time; ablations (multihead vs single-head, loss variants, loss-weight grid); deployment profiling (params, size FP32/FP16/INT8, FLOPs, GPU latency, peak memory); qualitative plots
metric_families: Curve Fréchet distance; Downstream classification; Efficiency (NFE / runtime / params); Pearson / correlation; RMSE; TSTR / TRTS; Visual inspection (qualitative)
eval_categories: Fidelity; Utility; Robustness; Clinical validity; Efficiency
robustness: Evaluated on two datasets with different sampling rates (public PTB-XL and private HeMI); wearable noise, motion artefact and device shift explicitly not modelled.
notes: 1T7 PTB-XL: RMSE 0.158, PCC 0.747, FD 0.739 vs SSSD-S4 0.163/0.737/0.825; 2T6 non-MI PCC 0.823 (PTB-XL), 0.846 (HeMI); MI harder than non-MI. Synthesized single leads give MI-detection F1 close to but below real leads (e.g. PTB-XL V2 80.5 vs 83.5); II+V1+III(syn) F1 84.8 vs II+V1 real 83.9. Generator 4.95 M params, 4.46 ms GPU. All similarity metrics paired; per-sample PCC SD ~0.2-0.3 shows large variance; 'expert judgment' visualisation is only figures; HeMI private.
takeaway: The disagreement between waveform metrics and diagnostic F1 argues for ECGEN-Eval to pair per-lead mae/RMSE and correlation with a downstream-utility hook, and to add a paired curve Fréchet distance distinct from the distributional fd metric to avoid name confusion.

title: Leveraging Statistical Shape Priors in GAN-Based ECG Synthesis
authors: Nour Neifar; Achraf Ben Hamadou; Afef Mdhaffar; Mohamed Jmaïel; Bernd Freisleben
model_family: GAN (conditional WGAN-GP generating statistical shape model parameters; 2D shape prior of temporal+amplitude variation; DTW-based k-means; LSTM discriminator)
task: class-cond (heartbeat classes N, V, F); augmentation
datasets: MIT-BIH Arrhythmia (MLII)
loss_functions: WGAN-GP (Wasserstein adversarial + gradient penalty, lambda=10)
loss_families: Adversarial (GAN); WGAN / gradient penalty
eval_metrics: RMSE; MAE; MSE; Earth Mover's Distance (EMD); DTW (ms); downstream precision/recall/F1 of three heartbeat classifiers in 5 augmentation settings; cardiologist visual Turing test (3 cardiologists, real vs synthetic and class identification)
metric_families: Augmentation gain; DTW; Expert / Turing test; Expert diagnostic agreement; MAE; MSE; RMSE; Wasserstein / EMD
eval_categories: Fidelity; Utility; Human / expert; Conditional consistency
notes: Includes useful literature table of metrics used by prior ECG GANs (MMD, DTW, FD, PRD, RMSE, PCC, DTW_D, MVDTW). Cardiologists recognized ~90-96.6% of real beats as real and classified synthetic classes correctly. Class F F1 rose to 0.93 with augmentation.
takeaway: Per-class metrics + small cardiologist Turing test; EMD in mV and DTW in ms are interpretable units worth reporting.

title: Lightweight Multi-task CNN for ECG Diagnosis with GRU-Diffusion
authors: Lehuai Xu; Zirui Lu; Haoran Yang; Yina Zhou
model_family: Diffusion (DDPM U-Net with embedded 16-layer GRU, 'GRU-Diffusion') + lightweight multi-task CNN classifier (DFNet)
task: augmentation (minority-class beats for classification)
datasets: MIT-BIH Arrhythmia (12 classes); PTB Diagnostic ECG Database (9 classes, 12 standard leads)
loss_functions: Generator: standard DDPM objective (not explicitly stated); classifier: cross-entropy for two tasks + L2 regularization
loss_families: L2 / MSE reconstruction; Diffusion noise prediction; Classification CE
eval_metrics: FID (Fréchet distance on PCA-reduced signals); mean and std of DTW on randomly paired real/generated signals; KL divergence between Welch PSDs; downstream Accuracy, Precision, Recall, F1; params/FLOPs
metric_families: Augmentation gain; DTW; Efficiency (NFE / runtime / params); FID / embedding Fréchet; Spectral / PSD similarity
embedding_extractor: PCA projection (no pretrained network)
notes: 'FID' computed on PCA features of raw signals, not an Inception/ECG network - naming inconsistency. Reports 99.72% (MIT-BIH) and 99.89% (PTB) accuracy. Uses both mean and std of random-pair DTW as diversity/alignment indicator.
takeaway: PSD-KL via Welch and DTW std (as spread indicator) are cheap complements; label PCA-based FD clearly as such.

title: MAGIC: Multi-Grained Conditional Diffusion for High-Fidelity PPG-to-ECG Translation
authors: Huixiang Wen; Shan Chang; Luo Zhou; Wei Liu; Jiaming Pei; Shengqun Jiang
venue: IEEE journal of biomedical and health informatics
model_family: Diffusion (1D Diffusion Transformer, v-prediction, cosine schedule T=500, classifier-free guidance w=3.5; PPG Transformer encoder with 4 global tokens via AdaLN + token-wise gated cross-attention; encoder pre-trained against paired ECG teacher)
task: PPG→ECG translation
datasets: WESAD; DaLiA; BIDMC; MIMIC-AFib (118 subjects total); downstream: PPG-BP (diabetes), Cuffless-BP (blood pressure)
loss_functions: diffusion v-prediction MSE; encoder pre-training: ROI-weighted (R-peak +-32 samples) ECG reconstruction MSE + InfoNCE contrastive PPG-ECG loss + stop-gradient latent alignment loss
loss_families: L2 / MSE reconstruction; Diffusion noise prediction; Physiology / physics; Contrastive / CLIP
eval_metrics: FD (Fréchet distance in learned feature space, RDDM protocol); RMSE (paired); HR MAE via Hamilton detector; AFib accuracy/F1 (VGG-13 on STFT spectrograms, pretrained on real MIMIC-AFib ECG); diabetes detection accuracy/F1 (VGG-11, PPG-BP); SBP/DBP MAE (1D-UNet on PPG + generated ECG); inference time vs steps; prediction-type and component ablations; qualitative visualisation
metric_families: Downstream classification; Efficiency (NFE / runtime / params); FID / embedding Fréchet; Heart rate / HRV; Other: downstream regression MAE; RMSE; Visual inspection (qualitative)
eval_categories: Fidelity; Utility; Robustness; Clinical validity; Conditional consistency; Efficiency
robustness: Evaluated across four heterogeneous datasets (lab, ambulatory with motion, ICU, AF), but no cross-dataset or subject-independent generalisation test.
embedding_extractor: not specified (FD 'in a learned feature space' following RDDM evaluation protocol)
notes: FD at T=500: MAGIC vs RDDM 2.88 vs 8.80 (WESAD), 0.52 vs 2.93 (DaLiA), 2.02 vs 6.54 (BIDMC), 0.69 vs 6.42 (MIMIC-AFib); RMSE mixed (0.16-0.27, RDDM better on several settings); HR MAE 3.28 / 4.74 bpm (WESAD/DaLiA); AFib acc 0.661 vs real ECG 0.706 (F1 0.675 vs RDDM 0.681); DBP MAE 1.34 vs 1.55 mmHg. Authors candidly note no significance testing, no multi-seed analysis, no cardiologist review, ROI mask needs ground-truth ECG, and that the FD feature extractor follows RDDM without specification; train/test subject split not described, so subject leakage cannot be ruled out.
takeaway: ECGEN-Eval's fed/fd should always state the embedding network explicitly (this paper's FD feature space is unspecified), and for paired translation tasks report FD alongside paired RMSE and an R-peak/HR consistency metric, since FD and RMSE rank models differently here.

title: MedFlow: Class-Aware Multi-Scale Generation for Medical Time-Series Synthesis
authors: Yanhao Huang; Shibo Feng; Wanjin Feng; Peilin Zhao; Chunyan Miao
model_family: FlowMatching (class-aware multi-scale flow matching over VQ multi-scale token embeddings with Token Marginal Guidance; MedFlow)
task: class-cond (medical time series incl. ECG; imbalanced classes)
datasets: MIMIC-III; eICU (EHR); APAVA (EEG); PTB Diagnostic ECG (Medformer split, 108/29/61 subjects)
loss_functions: Stage 1 tokenizer: MSE reconstruction + cosine commitment loss (EMA codebooks); Stage 2: categorical endpoint cross-entropy loss (class-weighted) + structured-source prior regularizer (no direct velocity regression)
loss_families: L2 / MSE reconstruction; Flow-matching velocity; Classification CE; VQ / codebook; Token cross-entropy
eval_metrics: TSTR AUROC; TSTR AUPRC; Discriminative Score (post-hoc GRU); Predictive Score; Context-FID (TS2Vec encoder, dim 320); t-SNE overlap; feature-wise moment, tail-quantile and minority-class statistic discrepancies; sampling throughput
metric_families: Classifier two-sample test; Efficiency (NFE / runtime / params); FID / embedding Fréchet; Membership inference / re-identification; Statistical tests; TSTR / TRTS; t-SNE / UMAP / PCA plots
eval_categories: Fidelity; Diversity; Utility; Privacy; Robustness; Efficiency
robustness: Downstream utility reported as mean over three independent evaluator seeds; component ablations. No noise or cross-dataset tests.
privacy: DOMIAS black-box membership-inference audit (segment- and subject-level MIR, subject-cluster bootstrap) on APAVA EEG only, not on the PTB ECG task.
embedding_extractor: TS2Vec encoder fitted on real data (Context-FID); GRU for discriminative/predictive scores
notes: For PTB ECG only TSTR AUROC/AUPRC reported; DS/PS/C-FID reported for EHR tasks. Claims avg -88.6% C-FID and 3.8x throughput vs TarDiff. Emphasises that global fidelity metrics can hide minority-class/tail failures.
takeaway: Add per-class / tail-quantile fidelity and Context-FID (TS2Vec) as a domain-agnostic embedding metric alongside ECG-specific FED.

title: Minority class-aware multiclass arrhythmia detection using conditional GAN augmentation
authors: Tiwari A, Kishore J, Singh R.
model_family: GAN (conditional WGAN-GP with auxiliary classifier in critic; 1D transposed-conv generator)
task: class-cond / augmentation (minority S and F beats)
datasets: MIT-BIH Arrhythmia (AAMI 5 classes N, S, V, F, Q)
loss_functions: Wasserstein adversarial loss + gradient penalty + auxiliary classifier (cross-entropy) loss in critic; downstream classifier cross-entropy
loss_families: Adversarial (GAN); WGAN / gradient penalty; Classification CE
eval_metrics: DTW; SSIM (synthetic vs real beats); visual P-QRS-T inspection; downstream hierarchical multi-stream / ResNet34 classifier accuracy, per-class and macro F1, per-class AUC/ROC, 5-fold cross-validation; inference latency, GFLOPs, memory, power on Jetson Nano/Raspberry Pi 5
metric_families: Augmentation gain; DTW; Efficiency (NFE / runtime / params); SSIM; Visual inspection (qualitative)
robustness: 5-fold cross-validation on augmented dataset; training stability/variance compared with baseline. Cross-dataset validation left to future work.
notes: Augmenting S and F to 10,000 each: macro F1 0.78 -> 0.94, F-class F1 +38%, S +28%. GAN checkpoint chosen by lowest critic loss and best downstream macro F1 on validation (selection on utility). Fidelity metrics (DTW, SSIM) only briefly reported.
takeaway: Utility via per-class minority F1 gains is the main signal; fidelity metrics are thin - typical of augmentation papers.

title: MM-DADM: Multimodal Drug-Aware Diffusion Model for Virtual Clinical Trials
authors: Qian Shao; Bang Du; Zepeng Li; Qiyuan Chen; Jiahe Chen; Hongxia Xu; Jimeng Sun; Jian Wu; Jintai Chen
model_family: Diffusion (DDPM backbone with pharmacokinetic ODE fusion via dynamic cross-attention + counterfactual drug-aware ControlNet-style CDC-Net; contrastive causal feature encoder)
task: other-modality2ECG / class-cond (drug- and demographics-conditioned post-dose ECG from pre-dose ECG; virtual clinical trials)
conditioning: Other ECG leads; Patient attributes (age, sex, ...); Class / diagnosis label; Physiological parameters / simulator
datasets: ECGRDVQ and ECGDMMLD (FDA drug trials; 9,443 12-lead ECGs, 44 subjects, 8 regimens)
loss_functions: DDPM epsilon-prediction MSE (L_bb, L_real) + lambda*causal guidance loss L_cau (1 - cosine sim to drug prototypes, lambda=0.1) for counterfactual samples; supervised contrastive loss L_con for the causal feature encoder
loss_families: L2 / MSE reconstruction; Diffusion noise prediction; Contrastive / CLIP
eval_metrics: accuracy/recall of normal-vs-abnormal status agreement on QTc (Bazett), PR, Tpeak-Tend intervals (single and multi-indicator); Fréchet ResNet Distance (FRD); RMSE; cardiologist real-vs-generated discrimination accuracy (10 cardiologists, 100 ECGs per lead per method); downstream ResNet-1D drug-administration classification with 100/200/500 synthetic augmentations
metric_families: Augmentation gain; Clinical intervals (PR/QRS/QT/ST); Expert / Turing test; FID / embedding Fréchet; RMSE; Visual inspection (qualitative)
eval_categories: Fidelity; Utility; Clinical validity; Human / expert; Conditional consistency
embedding_extractor: 1D ResNet pretrained on PhysioNet/CinC Challenge 2017 (final FC layer output) for FRD
notes: FRD 0.2431, RMSE 0.0127 vs SSSD-ECG 0.4719/0.0312 and FlowECG 0.5164. Expert Turing test: ideal is ~50% accuracy; MM-DADM near chance. Clinical-interval threshold agreement (normal/abnormal) is a novel clinically-grounded metric. Compares 10 baselines.
takeaway: Adopt FRD with a pretrained 1D ResNet, interval-category agreement (QTc/PR/Tpeak-Tend normal ranges), and a Turing-test protocol.

title: MorphDiff-ECG: A Diffusion Model for Multimodal Feature Fusion of ECG Signals
authors: Lei Zhang; Cheng Su; Mengying Ou; Mengyue Wang; Zhichao Xu; Shiyu Wei; Chang Liu; Tao Lei; Yong Wan
model_family: Diffusion (DDPM, x0-prediction; Transformer encoder + Feature Decoupling Enhancement with trend (polynomial), periodic (CWT top-M) and morphology (opening/closing) branches + SE-attention fusion; classifier-guided conditional sampling)
task: class-cond beat/segment generation (MIT-BIH N/A/V/L/R; CPSC2020 N/S/V; CPSC2018 9 classes); evaluated as reconstruction vs reference signals
datasets: MIT-BIH Arrhythmia (5 beat classes); CPSC2020 (N, S, V); CPSC2018 (9 classes, 6,877 records)
loss_functions: Timestep-weighted hybrid: time-domain L1/L2 reconstruction + CWT wavelet-coefficient loss + morphological opening/closing envelope loss (λp = λm = sqrt(L)/5)
loss_families: L1 reconstruction; L2 / MSE reconstruction; Spectral / frequency; Physiology / physics
eval_metrics: PRD; Fréchet distance in TS2Vec embedding space; RMSE; MAE; Pearson correlation; per-class and macro/sample-weighted averages; ablation; hyperparameter sensitivity; PCA latent visualisation; CWT spectrogram comparison; SE attention weights; parameters, inference and training time
metric_families: Efficiency (NFE / runtime / params); FID / embedding Fréchet; MAE; PRD / normalised PRD; Pearson / correlation; RMSE; Spectral / PSD similarity; t-SNE / UMAP / PCA plots
robustness: Hyperparameter sensitivity (diffusion steps, noise schedule, window, learning rate) with PRD varying 0.160-0.163; no signal-noise robustness test.
embedding_extractor: TS2Vec (self-supervised time-series encoder)
notes: MIT-BIH vs 17 baselines: PRD 53.965 (CECG-GAN 55.048), FD 0.738 (MC-WGAN better at 0.644), RMSE 0.207, MAE 0.165; Table IV PRD 0.118/0.135/0.021 and Pearson 0.940/0.920/0.986 for MIT-BIH/CPSC2020/CPSC2018. PRD/RMSE/MAE/Pearson are paired against reference signals (effectively reconstruction), scales differ across tables (PRD 53.965 vs 0.1609 vs 0.1181), the abstract attributes the headline gains to CPSC2020 while Table II is MIT-BIH, and many baselines are generic time-series models; several reference entries are unrelated papers, and no clinical-interval, expert or downstream-utility evaluation is reported.
takeaway: Uses an FD in TS2Vec embedding space, a candidate generic-encoder backbone for fd/fed alongside ECG foundation models; ECGEN-Eval reports should state whether PRD/RMSE/MAE are paired or nearest-neighbour and the PRD scale (fraction vs %), since mixing them makes comparisons like this one meaningless.

title: Morphology-preserving transfer-guided GAN with adaptive discriminative loss for robust and imbalanced ECG arrhythmia detection
authors: Majid Sepahvand; Beneen Dourgham Karim Al-Harizi; Maytham N. Meqdad
model_family: GAN (TG-MS-GAN: SinGAN-like multi-stage coarse-to-fine pyramid, N=4, deformable-conv generators, first stage initialised from a PTB-XL-pretrained reconstruction generator, spectrally normalised conv discriminators) + EfficientNetV2-S classifier
task: augmentation (minority-class beat/segment synthesis for imbalanced arrhythmia classification)
datasets: MIT-BIH Arrhythmia (Normal, AF, AFL, VF); Chapman-Shaoxing (Normal, AF, AFL, SVT); PTB-XL (5 superclasses); Fetal ECG simulated database (Normal, Other, Abnormal); PTB-XL also used for generator pre-training
loss_functions: GAN: hinge adversarial loss + discriminator feature-matching 'energy' loss + cross-scale L1 consistency + discriminator agreement term; classifier: weighted CE + exponentially decayed center loss + focal-style focusing term
loss_families: Adversarial (GAN); Least-squares / hinge GAN; L1 reconstruction; Perceptual / feature matching
eval_metrics: Pearson correlation; DTW; RMSE; PRD; cosine similarity; SNR (morphology preservation, real vs generated); visual overlay; downstream accuracy, precision, recall, Macro-F1, AUPRC, PR and F1-confidence curves, confusion matrices; augmentation ablation (none vs SMOTE vs single-scale GAN vs multi-stage GAN)
metric_families: Augmentation gain; Cosine similarity; DTW; Downstream classification; PRD / normalised PRD; PSNR / SNR; Pearson / correlation; RMSE; Visual inspection (qualitative)
robustness: Claims robustness/generalisation by reporting results on four datasets separately (not true cross-dataset transfer) and threshold-sensitivity curves; no noise or perturbation tests.
notes: Morphology: Pearson 0.987, cosine 0.992, DTW 0.041, RMSE 0.028 mV, PRD 2.13%, SNR 26.45 dB (pairing of 'corresponding' real and generated beats and sample count unspecified). Augmentation gain on Chapman: acc 0.934->0.976, Macro-F1 0.901->0.962, AUPRC 0.812->0.891 (SMOTE 0.947/0.918/0.844). Possible leakage: Fig. 1 states the augmented set (incl. synthetic) is split 60/20/20, contradicting the text's train-only augmentation; no distributional, diversity or memorisation metrics, and the generator is a multi-scale reconstruction model whose near-perfect similarity may reflect copying.
takeaway: Near-perfect paired PRD/Pearson from a reconstruction-style GAN should trigger an nn_dist memorisation check; ECGEN-Eval reports should state how pairs were formed and warn when synthetic data could have entered a test split.

title: ODE-Constrained Generative Modeling of Cardiac Dynamics for 12-Lead ECG Synthesis
authors: Yakir Yehuda; Kira Radinsky
model_family: GAN (MultiODE-GAN: WaveGAN-based WGAN with ODE (McSharry EDM) physics constraints)
task: class-cond (beat-level 12-lead, per abnormality) / augmentation
datasets: Georgia 12-Lead ECG Challenge (G12EC); PTB-XL; private LVSD dataset (real-world evaluation)
loss_functions: Wasserstein adversarial loss + λ_EUL·Euler Loss = intra-lead Euler loss (ODE residual vs McSharry EDM) + inter-lead Euler loss (Einthoven/derivative consistency), weighting δ=0.6
loss_families: Adversarial (GAN); WGAN / gradient penalty; Physiology / physics
eval_metrics: Downstream ResNet classifier specificity at fixed sensitivity (real vs real+synthetic, paired t-test); AUROC; AUPRC; inter-lead MSE (Einthoven law consistency); KL divergence and MMD in pretrained ResNet feature space; LVSD detection vs six cardiologists
metric_families: Augmentation gain; Cross-dataset / external validation; Inter-lead consistency; KL / JS divergence; MMD
robustness: Real-world evaluation on private LVSD clinical dataset; 5-fold cross-validation with paired t-tests.
embedding_extractor: pretrained ResNet-based ECG encoder (KL, MMD)
notes: Inter-lead Einthoven MSE is a physiology-consistency metric. Baselines: SimGAN-extended, SSSD-ECG. KL<0.5 and MMD<0.01 for all abnormalities. Augmentation-only (TRTR vs TR+S) evaluation; no TSTR.
takeaway: Add an Einthoven/Goldberger inter-lead consistency metric (e.g., MSE of I - (II - III)) for 12-lead synthetic data.

title: One model, dual tasks: a novel distributionally adaptive learning framework for ECG classification and generation addressing intra- and inter-patient variability
authors: Xinyi Wu; Zouheir Rezki; Bhavan Balusu; Jiaming Zhou; Jun Bai
model_family: GAN (AC-WGAN-GP: 7-block transformer generator conditioned on class label + 1D-CNN discriminator/classifier with L-Softmax; single-heartbeat test-time adaptation with entropy minimisation + minimum class confusion)
task: class-cond (beat augmentation for inter-patient arrhythmia classification)
datasets: MIT-BIH Arrhythmia (intra-patient 80/20 and de Chazal DS1/DS2 inter-patient split); MIT-BIH Supraventricular (SVDB); St Petersburg INCART
loss_functions: Wasserstein adversarial loss + gradient penalty (lambda 9) + auxiliary cross-entropy classification loss + large-margin softmax (L-Softmax, m=4); TTA: entropy minimisation + minimum class confusion
loss_families: Adversarial (GAN); WGAN / gradient penalty; Classification CE
eval_metrics: visual comparison of synthetic vs real beats per class; classification accuracy, per-class recall, precision, F1, AUROC, AUPRC, confusion matrices with/without synthetic augmentation + TTA on MITDB-DS2, SVDB, INCART; 10-run mean ± SD; inference time per heartbeat
metric_families: Augmentation gain; Cross-dataset / external validation; Downstream classification; Efficiency (NFE / runtime / params); Visual inspection (qualitative)
robustness: Inter-patient and cross-database evaluation (DS2, SVDB, INCART) with test-time adaptation; results likely inflated because synthetic beats are mixed into test sets.
privacy: TTA motivated as privacy-friendly (no target-data pooling); no privacy evaluation of the synthetic beats.
notes: Reports 99.86% intra-patient and 99.99% inter-patient accuracy (F1 ~0.9999 for all classes on DS2, SVDB, INCART), far above every prior inter-patient result, which is implausible. Synthetic beats from the generator are added to the external test sets during TTA (Fig. 5c: e.g. 3,008 N, 2,050 S, 388 F synthetic beats), so test metrics are computed partly on synthetic data - a likely leakage/inflation; synthetic-signal quality is assessed only by visual inspection, with no fidelity, distribution or diversity metric.
takeaway: A cautionary example: ECGEN-Eval documentation should require that utility tests keep synthetic samples strictly out of the real test set and report direct fidelity/diversity metrics (mmd, pr_dist, nn_dist) rather than inferring generator quality from near-perfect downstream accuracy.

title: Optimization of generative-adversarial networks for the synthesis of electrocardiograms by adaptive quantization
authors: Максим Михайлович Гордеев; A.E. Savkin; O. P. Timofeeva; Полина Анатольевна Шагалова
venue: Herald of Dagestan State Technical University Technical Sciences
model_family: GAN (MeGAN: BiLSTM generator, CNN discriminator) + post-training weight quantization (AGWR vs Min-Max)
task: unconditional; model compression
datasets: stated as MIT-BIH Arrhythmia (described as 10 s, 500 Hz, 12-lead, which is inconsistent with MIT-BIH)
loss_functions: standard GAN adversarial (BCE, sigmoid discriminator)
loss_families: Adversarial (GAN)
eval_metrics: Frechet Distance (Gaussian on feature space); PSNR; SSIM; Pearson correlation (quantized vs original model outputs); memory consumption
metric_families: Efficiency (NFE / runtime / params); FID / embedding Fréchet; PSNR / SNR; Pearson / correlation; SSIM
embedding_extractor: not specified ('feature space of the generated layer')
notes: Russian-language paper. FD: MeGAN 0.963 vs RNN-AE GAN 0.969, LSTM-VAE GAN 0.975; quantized 0.964 with ~75% memory reduction at 4-bit. Questionable claim that FD 0.9-1.0 indicates good quality; dataset description inconsistent. PSNR 29.81, SSIM 0.9427 compare quantized vs unquantized outputs.
takeaway: Example of FD values without stated embedding model; ECGEN-Eval should report extractor and scale for every Frechet metric.

title: PDE-Driven Spatiotemporal Generative Modeling for Multilead ECG Synthesis
authors: Yakir Yehuda; Kira Radinsky
venue: Proceedings of the AAAI Conference on Artificial Intelligence
model_family: GAN (PDE-based physics generator, 'PhysioPDE-GAN', reaction-diffusion SA/AV/HP subsystems over lead lattice)
task: class-cond 12-lead beat generation / augmentation
datasets: Georgia 12-Lead ECG Challenge (G12EC); PTB-XL (generalization)
loss_functions: Non-saturating adversarial loss + coupled PDE residual loss (forward-Euler derivative vs learned response, weighted per SA/AV/HP) + temporal gating loss (Frobenius penalty on activity outside P/PR/QRS-T masks); standard discriminator loss
loss_families: Adversarial (GAN); Physiology / physics
eval_metrics: Downstream classifier specificity at fixed sensitivity on real held-out test set (ResNet and attention-ResNet), real vs real+synthetic augmentation across baselines (DCGAN, WaveGAN, ME-GAN, MultiODE-GAN, SSSD-ECG); 5-fold cross-validated paired t-test; qualitative beat comparison
metric_families: Augmentation gain; Cross-dataset / external validation; Statistical tests; Visual inspection (qualitative)
robustness: Generalisation tested by repeating the augmentation study on PTB-XL besides G12EC; 5-fold cross-validation with paired t-tests.
notes: Only utility (TRTR vs augmented) evaluated; no direct fidelity/distribution metrics. Patient-wise split enforced. Reporting specificity at fixed sensitivity is a clinically interpretable protocol. NeuroKit2 for beat segmentation.
takeaway: Specificity-at-fixed-sensitivity augmentation protocol with paired t-tests is a good utility-evaluation template.

title: PENGUIN: General Vital Sign Reconstruction from PPG with Flow Matching State Space Model
authors: Shuntaro Suzuki; Shuitsu Koyama; Shinnosuke Hirano; Shunya Nagashima
model_family: FlowMatching (OT-CFM with dual-stream S5 state-space Flow-SSM blocks; Heun sampler, 25 steps)
task: PPG2ECG (also PPG->respiration, PPG->ABP)
data_type: Single-lead ECG; Wearable / ambulatory ECG; Multimodal (ECG + other signals)
datasets: PPG-DaLiA; WildPPG (ECG); BIDMC; WESAD (resp); UCI-BP; MIMIC-BP (ABP)
loss_functions: conditional flow matching loss (OT-CFM, L2 velocity regression)
loss_families: L2 / MSE reconstruction; Flow-matching velocity
eval_metrics: HR Error (MAE of heart rate in bpm, Hamilton detector, 8 s window); RR Error; SBP/DBP Error; qualitative waveform comparison; ablation
metric_families: Heart rate / HRV; Other: ablation; Visual inspection (qualitative)
eval_categories: Fidelity; Robustness; Clinical validity; Conditional consistency
robustness: Cross-subject 6:1:1 splits with no subject overlap on wearable datasets with motion artifacts (PPG-DaLiA, WildPPG).
notes: ECG reconstruction judged only by HR MAE (15.64 bpm DaLiA, 12.97 WildPPG) — no waveform-level metrics; cross-subject 6:1:1 split. Baselines: CycleGAN, RDDM, RespDiff, PaPaGei-S.
takeaway: Derived-physiology errors (HR MAE) are an easy clinical paired metric, but alone are insufficient for morphology.

title: Personalized Synthetic Electrocardiograms with Outcomes
authors: Jonas Lynggaard Isaksen; Vajira Lasantha Thambawita; Malene Nørregaard; Christina Ellervik; Torben F. Hansen; Allan R Linneberg; Dominik Linz; Claus Graff; Michael Alexander Riegler; Jørgen Kim Kanters
model_family: Other (U-Net denoising generator trained with MSE; GAN-derived without discriminator; personalized 1:1 synthesis from noisy original)
task: other (personalized 1:1 synthetic 12-lead ECG with linked patient characteristics and outcomes; privacy-preserving data sharing)
datasets: GESUS and LOFUS cohorts (training); Danish Inter99 cohort (testing, 6,612 ECGs)
loss_functions: Point-wise MSE between denoised output and original noise-free ECG (input = original + uniform noise 0-0.18 mV)
loss_families: L2 / MSE reconstruction
eval_metrics: Bland-Altman agreement of GE 12SL-measured markers (HR, QT, QTcF, QRS duration, PR, P-wave duration, P/R/T amplitudes in II, V1, V5, transition zone); linear-model associations of markers with sex, age, BMI; Cox-model hazard ratios for all-cause mortality; nearest-neighbour re-identification rate in normalized marker space (<=5% limit)
metric_families: Clinical intervals (PR/QRS/QT/ST); Demographic attribute preservation; Nearest-neighbour / DCR distance; Other: outcome association preservation
eval_categories: Fidelity; Utility; Privacy; Fairness; Robustness; Clinical validity
fairness: Tested preservation of ECG marker associations with sex, age and BMI; e.g. QTc ~9.5 ms shorter in men preserved in synthetic ECGs.
robustness: Trained on GESUS/LOFUS cohorts, evaluated on separate Danish Inter99 cohort.
privacy: Nearest-neighbour re-identification: 3.7% of synthetic ECGs had their source ECG as nearest neighbour in Euclidean marker space (limit 5%).
embedding_extractor: GE Marquette 12SL (FDA-cleared) ECG measurement algorithm
notes: Only 3.7% of synthetic ECGs had their source as nearest neighbour (privacy). Preserved QTc sex difference (~9.5 ms) and mortality HRs. PR associations attenuated; MSE loss underweights small P waves. Criticises MSE/Frechet-distance/visual validation as unsuitable; argues for domain-specific markers.
takeaway: Add epidemiological association-preservation tests and marker-space nearest-neighbour re-identification rate to ECGEN-Eval.

title: PG-LRF: Physiology-Guided Latent Rectified Flow for Electro-Hemodynamic PPG-to-ECG Generation
authors: Xiaoda Wang; Minxiao Wang; Kaiqiao Han; Defu Cao; Ching Chang; Yidan Shi; Runze Yan; Xiao Luo; Yan Liu; Xiao Hu; Yizhou Sun; Wei Wang; Carl Yang
model_family: FlowMatching (latent rectified flow, PPG-conditioned, physiology-aware VAE-style autoencoder + electro-hemodynamic ODE simulator guidance)
task: PPG2ECG
datasets: MC-MED (Stanford ED, 118,385 visits, 70,545 patients; official splits)
loss_functions: PAE: phase-delay consistency (circular squared PAT distance) + L2 reconstruction + beta*KL + global posterior alignment + bidirectional InfoNCE contrastive (instance) + cross-modal decodability L2; Flow: rectified-flow velocity MSE + simulator-guided Euler residual losses on ECG and induced PPG; simulator fitting: waveform + derivative + peak-alignment losses
loss_families: L2 / MSE reconstruction; Flow-matching velocity; KL / ELBO; Physiology / physics; Contrastive / CLIP
eval_metrics: MAE; RMSE; FD; FID; heart-rate MAE; fiducial MAE for PR, QRS, QT, QTcF, ST-J60 deviation, P-wave duration, T-wave duration (ms); downstream multi-label CVD detection AUROC (ICD I48, I71, I70, I44, I25, I50) and macro-AUROC; mean±SD over 3 runs
metric_families: Clinical intervals (PR/QRS/QT/ST); Curve Fréchet distance; Downstream classification; FID / embedding Fréchet; Heart rate / HRV; MAE; RMSE; Seed / run variability
eval_categories: Fidelity; Utility; Robustness; Clinical validity; Conditional consistency
robustness: All metrics reported as mean±SD over three runs; qualitative case showing preserved rhythm when reference ECG is noisy. No cross-dataset evaluation.
notes: vs PPGFlowECG: MAE 0.87->0.71, FID 44.17->37.79, HR MAE 7.08->3.94; PR error 59.9 ms, QT 29.3 ms. Macro-AUROC 0.633 vs PPG baseline 0.545. Large interval errors even for SOTA show limits of PPG2ECG.
takeaway: Fiducial-interval MAE panel (PR, QRS, QT, QTcF, ST-J60, P, T durations) and HR MAE map directly to ECGEN-Eval features module.

title: Physiology-Aware Benchmarking of Deep Generative Models for Fetal ECG Synthesis
authors: Yating Hu; Yu Lu; Wei Zhang; Shijie Shi; Junsong Wang
venue: Lecture notes in computer science (ICIC 2026, LNCS 16656)
model_family: EvalOnly (benchmark of TimeVAE, TimeGAN, Diffusion-TS and n-t-diffusion for unconditional fetal ECG generation, with a Signal-Distribution-Physiology evaluation framework)
task: evaluation (benchmark of unconditional fetal ECG generation)
datasets: ADDB (Abdominal and Direct Fetal ECG Database, 5 labour recordings, 1 kHz); BDDB (12 labour recordings, abdominal + direct FECG with reference annotations)
loss_functions: not applicable (models trained with their native objectives: ELBO, adversarial/supervised, diffusion denoising)
loss_families: Adversarial (GAN); KL / ELBO
eval_metrics: qualitative single-cycle QRS-T waveforms; t-SNE manifold overlap; Welch PSD plots; PCA-based FID; MSE; Wasserstein-1 (POT); histogram JS divergence; PSD KL divergence (0.5-40 Hz); real-vs-synthetic classifier AUC and Discrepancy score (1-accuracy); QRS duration via Pan-Tompkins + Daubechies-4 wavelet modulus maxima (constraint 30-80 ms); QRS waveform consistency (Pearson correlation to real QRS template); preprocessing sensitivity (min-max vs raw)
metric_families: Classifier two-sample test; Clinical intervals (PR/QRS/QT/ST); FID / embedding Fréchet; KL / JS divergence; MSE; Other: preprocessing sensitivity; Pearson / correlation; Spectral / PSD similarity; Wasserstein / EMD; t-SNE / UMAP / PCA plots
robustness: Cross-dataset consistency (ADDB vs BDDB) and preprocessing sensitivity analysis showing statistical metrics are scale-sensitive while QRS metrics are stable.
embedding_extractor: PCA on flattened raw segments (PCA-FID)
notes: ADDB: n-t-diffusion FID 0.016, classifier AUC 0.679 (Dis 0.50), QRS 30.7 ms, QRS consistency 0.607 vs TimeVAE FID 0.064 with QRS 23.3 ms and TimeGAN FID 1.25/AUC 1.00 (mode collapse); BDDB: n-t-diffusion FID 0.0035, QRS 32.0 ms was the only value inside 30-80 ms. Shows a 'statistical-physiological gap' (low MSE/FID with implausible QRS width), but QRS compliance is judged on the mean duration rather than a per-sample compliance rate, MSE is computed on unpaired samples, FID uses PCA features, raw-signal FID varies by 4 orders of magnitude, and there is no downstream utility test.
takeaway: Strong support for ECGEN-Eval's clinical feature extractor: report per-sample physiological-range compliance rates (e.g. % of beats with QRS in range) next to distribution metrics, and caveat that PCA-FID/MSE are scale-dependent and can favour over-smoothed generators.

title: PPG-to-ECG Signal Translation for Continuous Atrial Fibrillation Detection via Attention-based Deep State-Space Modeling

title: Principal component conditional generative adversarial networks for imbalanced ECG classification enhancement
authors: Chao Tang

notes: Explicit critique: RMSE/MAE/PRD are 'diluted' by many steady-state samples and depend on sampling rate; proposes range-normalized NPRD/NRMSE/NMAE. Also uses classifier-feedback sample filtering (keep samples only if metrics improve) - leakage risk.
takeaway: Adopt range-normalized NRMSE/NPRD/NMAE and consider QRS-weighted errors to counter dilution by isoelectric segments.

title: Quantum-Refined Latent Diffusion: A Hybrid Generative Framework for Imbalanced ECG Classification
authors: Georgios Kritopoulos; Georgios Neofotistos; Georgios D. Barmparis; Giorgos P. Tsironis
model_family: Hybrid (latent diffusion: spectral-guided cVAE + class-conditional latent DDPM with CFG + Quantum Latent Refinement via parameterized quantum circuits)
task: augmentation (class-cond minority beats S, V, F)
datasets: MIT-BIH Arrhythmia (44 records, AAMI classes; intra-patient temporal 80/10/10 split)
loss_functions: cVAE: MSE + L1 DFT-magnitude spectral loss + β-annealed KL (β→0.05); latent DDPM: noise-prediction MSE; QLR: stay loss ||z_refined − z_raw||² + MMD² (median-heuristic RBF) to real class latent bank; classifier: class-weighted CE
loss_families: L1 reconstruction; L2 / MSE reconstruction; Diffusion noise prediction; KL / ELBO; Spectral / frequency

embedding_extractor: cVAE latent space (32-d) for MMD
notes: Macro F1 0.747 baseline → up to 0.835 with augmentation. Fidelity measured only on class-mean waveforms (cosine sim misleading for multimodal V class, authors note). Intra-patient temporal split means same patients appear in train and test. MMD used both as training loss and eval metric (circularity risk).
takeaway: Use multi-bandwidth MMD rather than single kernel; avoid evaluating with the same metric used as training loss; mean-waveform similarity hides diversity.

title: RDiffGAN-ECG: High-quality specific R-peaks conditional ECG generation using denoising diffusion generative adversarial network with state space models
authors: Mingjun Lin; Xin Zhang; Yong Hong; Yaoqi Wen; Xueqi Lu; Qiucen Wu; Hongwen Chen; Chaomin Chen

metric_families: Classifier two-sample test; Curve Fréchet distance; DTW; Efficiency (NFE / runtime / params); Heart rate / HRV; RMSE; Visual inspection (qualitative); t-SNE / UMAP / PCA plots

Caveat: paired RMSE/FD/DTW compare against the real ECG whose R peaks condition RDiffGAN, while baselines get no R-peak input, so R-peak alignment alone favours the proposed model; HR match is partly by construction; no downstream utility test; generated MI/HYP amplitudes are lower than real.
takeaway: When generation is conditioned on fiducials taken from a real record, ECGEN-Eval reports should flag paired mae/dtw scores as conditioning-aligned and compare baselines with unpaired distributional metrics (fd, mmd, nn-based prd) plus heart_rate on held-out conditions.

title: rECG: A Guided Diffusion Framework for Remote Electrocardiography Reconstruction from Facial Video

Major caveats: ECG downsampled to 30 Hz (QRS morphology cannot be resolved), input segmentation and forward-diffusion noise masks use ground-truth ECG fiducials (possible leakage), train/test subject split not described, HR MAE equals RMSE in every row, and the skin-tone-diverse dataset is not used for any stratified/fairness analysis.

title: Reconstructing 12-Lead ECG from 3-Lead ECG using Variational Autoencoder to Improve Cardiac Disease Detection of Wearable ECG Devices

title: ReHeartNet: Reconstruct Electrocardiogram From Photoplethysmography by Using Dense Connected Deep Learning Model

title: Semi-supervised GAN for enhancing electrocardiogram time series diagnostics
authors: Dawei Li; Tienan Chen; Cong Liu; Liqi Liao; Shaoping Chen; Yongqiang Cui; Li Zhang; Yiyu Shi; Xiaowei Xu
model_family: GAN (TimeGAN-style: RNN embedding/recovery autoencoder + RNN generator and bidirectional RNN discriminator in latent space; GRU / LSTM / LSTM-LN cells)
task: class-wise synthesis for augmentation / class balancing (RBBB, RVOT, LVOT, Brugada, normal)

eval_metrics: t-SNE and PCA real vs synthetic; discriminative score (post-hoc RNN real-vs-synthetic classifier accuracy); predictive score (MAE of next-step predictor trained on synthetic, tested on real); ResNet-18 1D classification test accuracy, sensitivity, specificity (per class) with real, real+synthetic, synthetic-only training; comparison vs random oversampling, RCGAN, GES, Nef-Net
metric_families: Augmentation gain; Classifier two-sample test; TSTR / TRTS; t-SNE / UMAP / PCA plots
notes: Discriminative score 0.179 (GRU) / 0.238 (LSTM) / 0.193 (LSTM-LN), predictive MAE 0.022-0.027. Augmentation: Real 200 → Real+Syn 100+100 GRU accuracy 91.25 → 94.04%; synthetic-only 1000 GRU samples (TSTR) 97.2% vs real-553 92.1%, RCGAN 92.8%, GES 95.2%. Despite the title, this is a TimeGAN-like model, not a discriminator-as-classifier SGAN. Caveats: tiny private test set (100 records), patient counts inconsistent (653 vs 833), synthetic-only outperforming real is unexplained; no waveform or clinical fidelity metrics.
takeaway: ECGEN-Eval could add TimeGAN's discriminative score (post-hoc classifier two-sample test) and predictive score as optional metrics, and should report confidence intervals since tiny test sets like this make small accuracy gains uninterpretable.

title: Shape and amplitude decoupling in pulsatile physiological signal synthesis and its evaluation
authors: Kim J, Park K, Chen L, Kim K.
model_family: VAE (VABAM: variational framework with cascaded HPF/LPF filtering, bidirectional GRU, Gaussian shape latent z + uniform amplitude parameter theta); baselines ConVAE, FactorVAE, TCVAE, VDVAE, DiffWave, VDWave, WaveNet

eval_metrics: Five metrics: waveform shape factorization (SF), shape preservation / spectral distortion (SP/SD), amplitude modulation controllability (AC), spectral similarity (via conditional mutual information / KL on PSD permutation densities using FFT, DCT, Welch), reconstruction R2; composite ISCORE (arithmetic/geometric/harmonic mean of normalized metrics, Linfoot informational correlation normalisation)

notes: Nature Communications evaluation-oriented paper: introduces CMI-based PSD metrics and an aggregate ISCORE; shows ranking depends on PSD estimator (FFT/DCT/Welch) and aggregation mean, so they report all. SF excluded for non-factorized models (diffusion). 400k/50k/20k train/val/test per signal/dataset.
takeaway: Report spectral metrics under multiple PSD estimators and justify any composite score (AM/GM/HM sensitivity).

authors: Xiaoda Wang; Kaiqiao Han; Yuhao Xu; Xiao Luo; Yizhou Sun; Wei Wang; Carl Yang

title: Single-Lead ECG Arrhythmia Classification Based on Peak-Enhanced Attention Network and Quality-Aware GAN Data Augmentation Framework

eval_metrics: MSE; PRD; DTW; SSIM; FD-SIM (Fréchet-distance-based similarity); downstream 1D-CNN classification on MIT-BIH with 3000/5000 synthetic F beats added: F1 of F class, balanced accuracy, G-mean, macro F1; ablation (PGMA, spectral loss)
metric_families: Augmentation gain; DTW; MSE; Other: Fréchet-distance-based similarity; Other: ablation study; PRD / normalised PRD; SSIM
notes: SMA-GAN (5000 synth F beats): MSE 0.003, PRD 10.5%, DTW 0.034, SSIM 0.632, FD-SIM 0.999; F1-F 0.498 (no augmentation) -> 0.863, macro F1 0.837 -> 0.954 vs WGAN-GP 0.828/0.943. Pairing of synthetic vs real beats for MSE/PRD/DTW/SSIM is not described, FD-SIM's feature space is undefined and saturates (0.93-0.999 for every method), and results are single runs without variance; patient-independent split is a plus.
takeaway: Typical beat-level paper reporting paired-style MSE/PRD/DTW/SSIM with no stated pairing and a saturated Fréchet "similarity" — ECGEN-Eval's nearest-neighbour prd/mae/ssim plus a non-saturating fd/fed and a per-class augmentation-gain report would make such comparisons interpretable.

title: Spatially-Conditioned Variational Autoencoder with Latent Manifold Harvesting for High-Fidelity 12-Lead ECG Synthesis
authors: Ashutosh Mishra; Nicolas Stein; Louis Peter; Michael Guckert
model_family: VAE (spatially-conditioned cVAE with multi-resolution beat-position mask injection, nearest-neighbour upsampling; Latent Manifold Harvesting latent bank)

eval_metrics: visual side-by-side inspection; per-channel 1D-ResNet ensemble classifier applied to synthetic ECGs: Pearson correlation between predicted pathology prevalence and training distribution ('Ensemble Correlation'); Cumulative Mean Certainty / Reliability Score (mean |p-0.5|*2); reconstruction MSE; heuristic peak-alignment acceptance criteria
metric_families: Label / condition adherence; MSE; Physiological validity rate; Visual inspection (qualitative)
embedding_extractor: per-channel 1D-ResNet classifiers trained on real data
notes: Latent Manifold Harvesting: only latents whose decodings pass R-peak count/location/amplitude and baseline-smoothness tolerance are banked, then jittered (rejection sampling biases diversity). Per-lead independent VAEs ignore inter-lead consistency. Ensemble correlation r>=0.98 for AFIB, LBBB, AF; 100 samples per pathology; CPU-only training.
takeaway: Classifier label-prevalence correlation and confidence are cheap conditional-fidelity checks; peak-alignment heuristics could serve as a plausibility metric.

title: SSSD-ECG-nle: New Label Embeddings with Structured State-Space Models for ECG generation
authors: Sergey Skorik; Aram Avetisyan

notes: Key pitfall: good TSTR yet physicians identified synthetic ECGs almost perfectly (279/280 synthetic, 99/100 real correct); cues were low voltage, apparently reversed chest electrodes, artefacts. Authors dropped relation metrics (DTW, MMD, Wasserstein) and TSTS as 'uninformative'.
takeaway: TSTR alone is insufficient; add realism detectors (low-voltage, lead-reversal/inter-lead consistency checks) and a real-vs-synthetic classifier score.

notes: Conference abstract. Raw simulations harmed (AUC 0.93, AP 0.68); translated restored to baseline (AUC 0.95 vs 0.96, AP 0.81 vs 0.79). Notes clinicians recognise synthetic style; argues diffusion models offer objective convergence diagnostics vs unstable GANs.
takeaway: Report the 'harm' case: augmentation can degrade utility; include real-only baseline and AP for rare classes.

title: Synthesis of Multimodal Cardiological Signals Using a Conditional Wasserstein Generative Adversarial Network
authors: Ioana Crețu; Alexander Tindale; Wamadeva Balachandran; Maysam Abbod; Ashraf William Khir; Hongying Meng
model_family: GAN (MC-WGAN: conditional WGAN-GP, 1D U-Net generator with 6 down/6 up blocks and label embedding, 6-layer 1D-conv critic)
task: class-cond multimodal beat synthesis (ECG + ABP + CVP jointly; rhythm classes N, F, T, L, paced P); ECG-only on MIT-BIH for benchmarking
datasets: Private Harefield Hospital ICU dataset (29 patients, PACESIM trial: ECG V1 + invasive ABP + CVP, sinus/AF/AT/LBBB/paced); MIT-BIH Arrhythmia (lead II, AAMI classes N, A, V, R, L)

metric_families: Curve Fréchet distance; DTW; MAE; MMD; MSE; PRD / normalised PRD; RMSE; Visual inspection (qualitative)
notes: Private data, all signals/classes: RMSE 0.319, PRD 33.2, FD 0.490, DTW 3.27, MMD 0.469; ECG RMSE 0.248, PRD 25.1; CVP worst (PRD 48.3). MIT-BIH: RMSE 0.205, MAE 0.146, PRD 20.5, FD 0.225, DTW 1.355, MMD 0.0051 vs BC-GAN PRD 33.8, SynSigGAN PRD 6.3. Distances are averaged over all real beats (not nearest neighbour), cross-paper comparisons use different protocols, and no cross-modal consistency (e.g. ECG-ABP pulse transit delay), diversity or utility evaluation is done despite the multimodal claim.
takeaway: For multimodal or multi-channel generation ECGEN-Eval should add a cross-channel coupling check (e.g. R-peak to pressure-upstroke delay distribution) and state clearly whether paired metrics use nearest-neighbour or all-pairs averaging, since the two give very different numbers.

title: Synthetic Data Generation via Generative Adversarial Networks in Healthcare: A Systematic Review of Image- and Signal-Based Studies

title: Synthetic ECG Generation for Data Augmentation and Transfer Learning in Arrhythmia Classification
authors: José Fernando Núñez; Jamie Arjona; Javier Béjar
model_family: Diffusion (DiffWave/SSSD-ECG; Time-Diffusion = HF Diffusers Unet1D conditional) + VQ-VAE/MaskGIT (Time-VQVAE, TimeVQVAE)

Augmentation gains negligible per dataset, positive on merged set. Time-VQVAE best for fine-tuning but still below real-only.
takeaway: Add a classifier two-sample test (C2ST) and full TrRTeR/TSTR/TRTS/TrRSTeR matrix; MMD alone is underpowered.

title: Synthetic ECG signal generation using generative neural networks
authors: Edmond Adib; Fatemeh Afghah; John Jeffery Prevost
model_family: GAN (comparison of 5 models: Classic FC GAN, DC-DC GAN, BiLSTM-DC GAN, AE/VAE-DC GAN hybrid, WGAN)

eval_metrics: DTW, Frechet and Euclidean distances to template; Method 1 mean all-pairs set distance; Method 2/3 distances to random or expert-selected template (min distance); Method 4 productivity rate (% accepted beats under distance threshold); Method 5 expert visual inspection; ResNet34 augmentation precision/recall/F1/accuracy and confusion matrices

notes: Introduces threshold, accepted beat, productivity rate concepts. Euclidean distance unsuitable: a beat with minimum Euclidean distance lacked all morphological features. DTW and discrete Frechet agree; Frechet is a true metric. Classic GAN 72.3% productivity (DTW). Template choice (SAB vs expert-picked) affects scores. Includes table of prior ECG-GAN metrics.
takeaway: Acceptance/productivity rate under a DTW threshold is a practical metric; avoid plain Euclidean for morphology.

title: Synthetic ECG signals generation: A scoping review
authors: Beatrice Zanchi; Giuliana Monachino; Luigi Fiorillo; Giulio Conte; Angelo Auricchio; Athina Tzovara; Francesca D. Faraci
model_family: Survey (79 studies to Jan 2024: mathematical modelling — physiological, morphological, dynamic/ECGSYN; computer-vision-inherited augmentation — geometric, jitter, warping, filtering; deep generative models — VAEs, vanilla/recurrent/DC/conditional/progressive GANs, VAE-GAN hybrids, diffusion)
task: survey
conditioning: None (unconditional); Class / diagnosis label; Other ECG leads; Patient attributes (age, sex, ...); Physiological parameters / simulator
data_type: 12-lead clinical ECG; Single-lead ECG; Reduced-lead ECG (2-9 leads); Wearable / ambulatory ECG
data_format: Raw waveform segment; Single heartbeats; Long recording (>30 s); Time-frequency (spectrogram / wavelet); ECG image
datasets: 79 reviewed studies (Web of Science search, 823 hits); datasets catalogued include MIT-BIH Arrhythmia, NSRDB, AFDB, NSTDB, PTB-XL, PhysioNet/CinC 2017/2020/2021, CPSC2018, Chapman (CHINA), CCDD, GESUS, CUDB, VFDB, EPHNOGRAM
loss_functions: not applicable (survey)
eval_metrics: Catalogue (Fig. 13): visual inspection; increase in downstream/auxiliary classifier performance (ICP); MSE-based (MSE, NMSE, RMSE, NRMSE, PRD); MMD-based (MMD, KMMD, KID); FD-based (Fréchet distance, FID); time-warping (DTW, soft-DTW, TWED); Pearson correlation; Euclidean distance; MAE; MRE; SSIM; SNR; relative entropy/KL; EMD; Chamfer distance; t-SNE; statistics of ECG feature distributions (RR, QT, PR, QRS, axes); Poincaré plot; DFA; training-performance metrics (discriminator accuracy, loss convergence); template-based CI/FI comparison; real-vs-noise baselines; GAN-train/GAN-test (TSTR/TRTS); clinical Turing tests
metric_families: Augmentation gain; Classifier two-sample test; Clinical intervals (PR/QRS/QT/ST); DTW; Euclidean distance; Expert / Turing test; FID / embedding Fréchet; Heart rate / HRV; KL / JS divergence; MMD; Other: reference-baseline comparison; PRD / normalised PRD; Pearson / correlation; TSTR / TRTS; Visual inspection (qualitative); Wasserstein / EMD; t-SNE / UMAP / PCA plots
eval_categories: Fidelity; Diversity; Utility; Privacy; Fairness; Clinical validity; Human / expert
fairness: Mentions that increasing representation of underrepresented subsets can mitigate bias, but no fairness evaluation is reviewed.
privacy: Discusses anonymisation (HIPAA, GDPR, nFADP) and ECG as a biometric identifier as an emerging motivation for DGMs; no privacy metrics are catalogued.
notes: Classifies 79 works by technique, lead count, beat count and purpose; deep generative models are mostly used for augmentation, MM for modelling/device testing, CVIM for fast augmentation. Key evaluation conclusion: no standardized metric set exists, metrics are implemented and paired inconsistently (all-pairs, template-based, real-vs-real baselines), MSE-based metrics dominate followed by MMD, FD and DTW, so cross-study comparison is impossible; calls for pipelines combining quantitative, clinically relevant and expert assessment and for similarity metrics that do not penalise legitimate variability.
takeaway: Directly supports ECGEN-Eval's purpose; the report should group metrics into distributional vs paired families, always show a real-vs-real (held-out) reference for every metric, and add clinical feature-distribution comparisons (RR, QT, PR, QRS) as first-class metrics.

title: Synthetic Electrocardiogram Spectrogram Generation Using Generative Adversarial Network‐Based Models: A Comparative Study
authors: Giovanny Barbosa‐Casanova; Norelli Schettini; Winston Percybrooks; Begonya García-Zapirain

metric_families: Augmentation gain; Diversity / mode-collapse measure; Efficiency (NFE / runtime / params); FID / embedding Fréchet; Visual inspection (qualitative)

title: Synthetic electrocardiograms for Brugada syndrome: from data generation to expert cardiologists evaluation
authors: Beatrice Zanchi; Giuliana Monachino; Francesca Dalia Faraci; Matteo Metaldi; Pedro Brugada; Georgia Sarquella‐Brugada; Elijah Raphael Behr; Josép Brugada; Lia Crotti; Bernard Belhassen; Giulio Conte

notes: Experts at chance or worse: accuracy 40%/42%, specificity 22%/26%, sensitivity 58%; kappa −0.12 to 0.80. Bias toward calling ECGs real. Same display settings (25 mm/s, 10 mm/mV). Raises disclosure/watermarking concerns.
takeaway: Expert Turing-test protocol (blinded, repeated rounds, kappa) is a template; report specificity separately since raters are biased to 'real'.

title: Text-to-ECG: a Framework to Generate 12-Lead ECG from Text Reports
authors: Fabrizio Cattozzo; Sara Battiston; Massimo W. Rivolta; Roberto Sassi
venue: Annual International Conference of the IEEE Engineering in Medicine and Biology Society. IEEE Engineering in Medicine and Biology Society. Annual International Conference
model_family: GAN (conditional WGAN-GP; 1D upsample-conv generator, 2D-conv critic; frozen Bio_ClinicalBERT 768-d text embedding + 300-d uniform noise)
task: text-conditional (12-lead single heartbeat from short English diagnosis text; 5 classes NORM, IMI, ASMI, LAFB, LVH)
datasets: PTB-XL (100 Hz version; 29,391 balanced heartbeats; ~25 hand-written English report variants per class)
loss_functions: WGAN-GP critic loss (lambda=10) + generator Wasserstein loss; Gaussian instance noise (0.001 mV) added to critic inputs
loss_families: WGAN / gradient penalty
eval_metrics: UMAP projection of real (KDE heatmap) vs synthetic beats per class; GAN-train (TSTR / train-synthetic test-synthetic) and GAN-test (TRTS) per-class F1 and accuracy; per-timepoint 90% confidence-band overlap IoU per lead; visual comparison with cross-correlation-matched real beat
metric_families: Label / condition adherence; Other: per-timepoint confidence-band overlap (IoU); TSTR / TRTS; Visual inspection (qualitative); t-SNE / UMAP / PCA plots
notes: GAN-train: classifier trained on synthetic reaches 0.92 accuracy on synthetic but 0.60 on real (IMI F1 0.43) -> limited diversity; GAN-test: real-trained classifier 0.84 on real vs 0.72 on synthetic (ASMI F1 0.55, IMI 0.56); 90% band IoU 0.73-0.80 per class. UMAP shows ASMI samples landing in the IMI region (class confusion). No cardiologist evaluation despite abstract wording; authors note any fixed metric can be gamed and evaluation remains open.
takeaway: The per-lead 90% confidence-band IoU is a cheap, interpretable class-conditional envelope-overlap metric that ECGEN-Eval could add for aligned beats, alongside reporting GAN-train/GAN-test (TSTR/TRTS) pairs to separate diversity from fidelity.

title: Towards High-Fidelity ECG Generation: Evaluation via Quality Metrics and Human Feedback
authors: Maria Mourão Gonçalves Russo; Hugo Filipe Silveira Gamboa
venue: International Joint Conference on Biomedical Engineering Systems and Technologies (BIOSTEC)
model_family: Diffusion (SSSD-ECG: conditional diffusion with S4 layers, hyperparameter-tuned, conditioned on 5 PTB-XL diagnostic superclasses); GAN (1D DC-style CNN GAN, used only to make low-quality Class 2 signals for the quality dataset)
task: class-cond 12-lead generation / evaluation (new sample-level evaluator model + human feedback)
datasets: PTB-XL (via PhysioNet/CinC Challenge 2021); custom 4-class Quality Dataset (basic waveforms, GAN outputs, SSSD-ECG outputs, real PTB-XL)
loss_functions: GAN: binary cross-entropy for generator and discriminator; SSSD-ECG training loss not stated; evaluator classifier: class-weighted cross-entropy
loss_families: Adversarial (GAN); Classification CE
eval_metrics: improved precision; improved recall; density; coverage (k=5, TSFEL features); TSTR; TRTS; TSTS (Random Forest, macro F1); clinician real-vs-synthetic questionnaire with diagnostic class and quality-level follow-ups; evaluator model (5-CNN ensemble assigning 4 quality levels, % predicted Class 4); Pearson correlation of evaluator with precision/recall/density/coverage; evaluator vs. expert agreement
metric_families: Expert / Turing test; Expert diagnostic agreement; Other: learned quality evaluator; Other: metric agreement analysis; Other: quality-level grading; Precision / recall / density / coverage; TSTR / TRTS
eval_categories: Fidelity; Diversity; Utility; Human / expert; Conditional consistency
embedding_extractor: TSFEL (statistical, spectral and temporal handcrafted features)
notes: Extracted from the author's Dec 2024 MSc thesis (NOVA Lisbon), the basis of this paper; details may differ from the published version. Best hyperparameters raised mean precision 0.57->0.94, density 0.80->3.85, coverage 0.19->0.89, but recall stayed ~0.03; RF macro-F1: TRTR 56.58%, TRTS 57.03%, TSTR 40.84%, TSTS 78.00%. Majority vote of 3 clinicians judged 8/10 synthetic ECGs as real (2/10 real judged synthetic), but diagnostic labels for synthetic ECGs lacked consensus; evaluator correlated with precision (r=0.88) and density (r=0.72). Extracted from Maria Russo's Dec 2024 NOVA Lisbon MSc thesis, not the 2025 BIOSTEC paper (doi 10.5220/0013400500003911); human evaluation used signals from the original-hyperparameter model.
takeaway: Include a per-sample learned quality/realism grader alongside distribution-level precision, recall, density and coverage, and report recall and coverage together, because they can disagree sharply (0.03 vs 0.89).

title: TransDiffECG: Semantically controllable ECG synthesis via transformer-based diffusion modeling
authors: Yuxin Lin; Jing Ma; Suyu Dong; Chaoyu Sun; Wanting Cong; Kuanquan Wang; Gongning Luo; Wei Wang
model_family: Diffusion (DDPM on SSSD-ECG backbone; Transformer encoder/decoder blocks + Semantic ECG Batch Normalization (SPADE-like) conditioning on P/QRS/T segmentation masks)
task: semantic-mask-conditional (fiducial-level control of P/QRS/T placement, heart rate 50-110 bpm, QTc 330-495 ms); augmentation
datasets: QTDB (single-lead); LUDB (12-lead, patient-wise 5-fold CV); AF vs normal classification on LUDB
loss_functions: DDPM noise-prediction MSE
loss_families: L2 / MSE reconstruction; Diffusion noise prediction
eval_metrics: MMD; Pearson correlation (paired with mask-matched ground truth); U-Net P/QRS/T onset/offset precision and recall under AAMI EC57 tolerances for Real->Synthetic and Synthetic->Real segmentation; AF vs normal AUROC with augmentation (XResNet1d50, 5-fold); qualitative controllability of HR and QTc; membership inference attack AUROC; ablation
metric_families: Augmentation gain; Fiducial / R-peak timing; Label / condition adherence; MMD; Membership inference / re-identification; Pearson / correlation; TSTR / TRTS
eval_categories: Fidelity; Utility; Privacy; Robustness; Clinical validity; Conditional consistency
robustness: Notes sensitivity to noisy/implausible input masks as an unaddressed limitation; per-fold AUROC variability attributed to only 15 AF patients in LUDB.
privacy: Membership inference attack AUROC ~0.5 on both datasets; authors also argue moderate Pearson correlation (0.37/0.62) shows no copying, which is a weak memorization test.
notes: LUDB: MMD 3.21e-2 vs DiffECG 3.49e-2, SSSD-ECG 5.74e-2, P2PGAN 24.47e-2; PC 0.6177 vs 0.4866/0.3995. QTDB S->R segmentation ~98% onset/offset precision/recall (real 97-98.6%); AF AUROC 0.9451 with augmentation vs 0.9004 real-only; MIA AUROC 0.49 (QTDB)/0.51 (LUDB). Caveats: baselines were re-conditioned on masks by the authors; PC is computed against the ground-truth record whose mask was used (paired, so it measures conditional reconstruction) and is also misused as a memorization check; HR/QTc controllability shown only visually; no expert review.
takeaway: For mask/fiducial-conditioned generators, ECGEN-Eval's feature extractor could provide a conditional-adherence metric (delineated onsets/offsets or HR/QTc of synthetic vs requested values, with AAMI-style tolerances), and reports should flag paired Pearson as a reconstruction rather than distribution metric.

title: Transformer-Based Generative Adversarial Network With Multi-Scale Temporal Attention for ECG Synthesis and PQRST Feature Preservation
authors: Ayswarya R Kurup; Mithun Kumar Kar; Madhusudhan Mishra; Soumyabrata Dev; Debanga Raj Neog
model_family: GAN (TransGAN: Transformer generator with temporal self-attention, positional encoding and Swish; hierarchical multi-scale transformer patch discriminator at beat/rhythm/sequence windows; PQRST-constrained loss via adaptive peak detection)
task: unconditional (noise→10 s ECG) for augmentation with class-weighted loss
datasets: MIT-BIH Arrhythmia; PTB-XL; a simulated ('synthetic') ECG dataset
loss_functions: adversarial BCE + weighted BCE (class-frequency weights) in discriminator + lambda_PQRST x PQRST feature-consistency loss + temporal coherence constraint
loss_families: Adversarial (GAN); Spectral / frequency; Physiology / physics

authors: Majid Sepahvand; Maytham N. Meqdad

eval_metrics: downstream Accuracy, macro-P/R/F1, AUPRC; minority-class recall with/without augmentation; augmentation-strategy comparison (none, oversampling, SMOTE, single-stage cGAN); DTW and Pearson per stage on 200 DTW-matched real/synthetic beat pairs; QRS-duration deviation, P-wave presence rate, R-amplitude deviation; nearest-neighbour DTW to train vs held-out test (memorisation check); cross-dataset transfer; 5-seed 95% CI

Caution: the paper itself states the results are 'preliminary ... to illustrate the intended evaluation protocol' with 'full empirical validation on real training runs' left for future work, and there are internal inconsistencies (T=100 vs 150-sample beats), so numbers should not be treated as validated evidence.
takeaway: The protocol is a good template even if the numbers are unvalidated: ECGEN-Eval's nn_dist should report the train-vs-held-out nearest-neighbour distance gap explicitly, and the clinical feature extractor should report per-feature deviations (QRS duration ms, P-wave presence rate, R-amplitude %) between real and synthetic sets.

No augmentation significantly beats real-only macro F1 0.321 after Bonferroni; constrained keeps V-F1 0.651 vs 0.598 unconstrained. Only 13% of validated beats pass a local-smoothness audit; MIA accuracy 52.4%.
